name: kvkk-en
description: PRD §7.1 TR-Domain + TR-Adversarial, parallel EN half. Law No. 6698 (KVKK, consolidated with the 2024 Law 7499 amendments) and three KVKK regulations (erasure/destruction/anonymisation, data controllers' registry, 2024 transfer abroad), one file per article, article-aligned with kvkk-tr: the same filename is the same provision and the same query id is the same question. Built for the cross-lingual calibration experiment (PRD G5): language is the only thing that differs between the two sets. Queries drafted by Claude (Anthropic) with verbatim evidence checked mechanically; status=draft until verified by a person (make review DATASET=kvkk-tr PARALLEL=kvkk-en). kvkk-x-* are 150 adversarial queries whose answer is deliberately absent. Sources and licences: SOURCES.md.

queries.text: Which fundamental right does the KVKK primarily aim to protect?
evidence: to protect fundamental rights and freedoms of persons, particularly the right to privacy
queries.answer: The right to privacy (among the fundamental rights and freedoms of persons).
queries.note: Easy; purpose clause. 'özel hayatın gizliliği' also mentioned in art. 28 as a limit, not as the Law's purpose.

queries.text: Does the Law only protect individuals' rights, or does it also lay down rules for the companies processing the data?
evidence: to set forth obligations, principles and procedures which shall be binding upon natural or legal persons who process personal data
queries.answer: Both: it also sets the obligations, principles and procedures binding on natural or legal persons who process personal data.
queries.note: Purpose clause second limb; question avoids the word 'amaç'.

queries.text: Are customer records kept in paper files also covered by the KVKK?
evidence: by non-automated means which provided that form part of a data filing system
queries.answer: Yes, non-automated processing is covered provided the data form part of a data filing system.
queries.note: Casual/no diacritics. Paper files = non-automated means; condition is being part of a data filing system. Same phrase appears in the 'processing' definition (art. 3(e)).

queries.text: Does the KVKK also protect legal persons whose data are processed (e.g. a company's own information)?
evidence: The provisions of this Law shall apply to natural persons whose personal data are processed
queries.answer: No; the Law applies to natural persons whose personal data are processed; legal persons are covered only as processors of data.
queries.note: Tests that protected persons are natural persons only; legal persons appear only as processors.

queries.text: Is an insurance company that processes customer data entirely through automated systems subject to the KVKK?
evidence: natural or legal persons processing such data wholly or partially by automated means
queries.answer: Yes; the Law applies to natural or legal persons processing data wholly or partially by automated means.
queries.note: Scope for automated processing by a legal person.

queries.text: What three qualities must consent have to count as explicit consent?
evidence: means freely given, specific and informed consent
queries.answer: It must be freely given, specific and informed.
queries.note: Definition of explicit consent is unique to art. 3; three elements.

queries.text: Under the Law, what is a call-centre company that processes customer data on the bank's behalf and upon its authorization called?
evidence: means the natural or legal person who processes personal data on behalf of the data controller upon its authorization
queries.answer: A data processor.
queries.note: Role classification from a scenario; identical definition in the transfer by-law (aktarim art. 4).

queries.text: What does the Law call the party that determines the purposes and means of processing and sets up and manages the data filing system?
evidence: the natural or legal person who determines the purposes and means of processing personal data and is responsible for the establishment and management of the data filing system
queries.answer: The data controller.
queries.note: Definition repeated verbatim in all three by-laws, so all are relevant.

queries.text: For a dataset to count as anonymized, must it be impossible to link to a person even when matched with other data?
evidence: rendering personal data impossible to link with an identified or identifiable natural person, even through matching them with other data
queries.answer: Yes; it must be impossible to link it to an identified or identifiable natural person even through matching with other data.
queries.note: Anonymization test; same definition in the erasure by-law art. 10.

queries.text: Can a corporate (legal person) customer be a 'data subject' within the meaning of the KVKK?
evidence: means the natural person, whose personal data are processed
queries.answer: No; the data subject is the natural person whose personal data are processed.
queries.note: Data subject = natural person only; same definition in transfer by-law.

queries.text: Must a person's identity be known with certainty for information to count as personal data?
evidence: means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person
queries.answer: No; any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person is personal data.
queries.note: Identifiable vs identified; definition repeated in two by-laws.

queries.text: Does merely storing or classifying data count as 'processing of personal data'?
evidence: storage, protection, alteration, adaptation, disclosure, transfer, retrieval, making available for collection, categorization
queries.answer: Yes; any operation such as storage, protection or categorization performed on the data is processing.
queries.note: Long enumerated definition; answer buried mid-list. Repeated in two by-laws.

queries.text: How must data be organised for a record system to count as a 'data filing system' under the Law?
evidence: the system where personal data are processed by being structured according to specific criteria
queries.answer: Personal data must be processed by being structured according to specific criteria.
queries.note: Data filing system definition; also in erasure by-law art. 4.

queries.text: What general principles must be complied with when processing personal data?
evidence: Lawfulness and fairness
Being accurate and kept up to date where necessary
Being processed for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes
Being relevant, limited and proportionate to the purposes for which they are processed
Being stored for the period laid down by relevant legislation or the period required for the purpose for which the personal data are processed
queries.answer: Lawfulness and fairness; accuracy and being up to date where necessary; specified, explicit and legitimate purposes; relevant, limited and proportionate; stored only for the period required.
queries.note: List question: all five principles. Erasure by-law art. 7 only refers to art. 4 without listing.

queries.text: Under the Law, for how long may we keep customer data?
evidence: Being stored for the period laid down by relevant legislation or the period required for the purpose for which the personal data are processed
queries.answer: For the period laid down by relevant legislation or the period required for the purpose of processing.
queries.note: Retention period; distractor: erasure by-law defines policy 'azami süre' and art. 16 registry field.

queries.text: Is keeping customer address data up to date a requirement arising from the Law?
evidence: Being accurate and kept up to date where necessary
queries.answer: Yes; data must be accurate and kept up to date where necessary.
queries.note: Accuracy principle; 'where necessary' qualifier.

queries.text: Is collecting more data than needed for a loan application contrary to the Law?
evidence: Being relevant, limited and proportionate to the purposes for which they are processed
queries.answer: Yes; data must be relevant, limited and proportionate to the purposes of processing.
queries.note: Casual/no diacritics. Data minimisation phrased as a scenario.

queries.text: Is personal data processed only under the KVKK, or are procedures in other laws binding as well?
evidence: Personal data shall only be processed in compliance with procedures and principles laid down in this Law or other laws.
queries.answer: Data may only be processed in compliance with the procedures and principles of this Law or other laws.
queries.note: Art. 4(1): processing must comply with KVKK and other laws.

queries.text: Is it compliant with the principles to define the processing purpose in vague, general terms?
evidence: Being processed for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes
queries.answer: No; data must be processed for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes.
queries.note: Purpose limitation, negative phrasing.

queries.text: As a general rule, what is needed to process a customer's personal data?
evidence: Personal data shall not be processed without explicit consent of the data subject.
queries.answer: The data subject's explicit consent; personal data shall not be processed without it (exceptions in art. 5(2)).
queries.note: Default rule; distractor: art. 8(1) states same rule for transfers, art. 6 for special categories.

queries.text: When processing a customer's identity data to conclude a loan agreement, do we also need explicit consent?
evidence: Processing of personal data of the parties of a contract is necessary, provided that it is directly related to the establishment or performance of the contract.
queries.answer: No; processing the contracting parties' data is allowed without consent if directly related to establishing or performing the contract.
queries.note: Contract performance ground; distractor art. 9(6)(b) for transfers abroad.

queries.text: Does processing data to comply with a legal obligation the bank is subject to require explicit consent?
evidence: It is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which the data controller is subject.
queries.answer: No; consent is not required where processing is necessary for compliance with the controller's legal obligation.
queries.note: Legal obligation ground.

queries.text: What condition applies to processing data without explicit consent on the basis of legitimate interest?
evidence: Processing of data is necessary for the legitimate interests pursued by the data controller, provided that this processing shall not violate the fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject.
queries.answer: It must be necessary for the controller's legitimate interests and must not violate the data subject's fundamental rights and freedoms.
queries.note: Legitimate interest and its balancing condition.

queries.text: May we process (non-special) information that the customer has made public himself/herself without obtaining explicit consent?
evidence: Personal data have been made public by the data subject himself/herself.
queries.answer: Yes; data made public by the data subject may be processed without explicit consent.
queries.note: Made-public ground for ordinary data; distractors: art. 6(3)(ç) (special data, extra condition) and art. 28(2)(b).

queries.text: Can the personal data of an unconscious insured person be processed without consent to protect his/her life?
evidence: It is necessary for the protection of life or physical integrity of the person himself/herself or of any other person, who is unable to explain his/her consent due to the physical disability or whose consent is not deemed legally valid.
queries.answer: Yes; where necessary to protect the life or physical integrity of a person unable to give consent due to physical disability.
queries.note: Vital interests ground; same wording in art. 6(3)(c) and 9(6)(e), but question is about ordinary processing.

queries.text: Does processing a customer's data to protect our right in a debt-collection lawsuit require explicit consent?
evidence: Data processing is necessary for the establishment, exercise or protection of any right.
queries.answer: No; processing necessary for the establishment, exercise or protection of a right may be done without consent.
queries.note: Establishment/exercise/protection of a right.

queries.text: Is customer consent needed for processing that is expressly provided for by law?
evidence: Personal data may be processed without seeking the explicit consent of the data subject only in cases where one of the following conditions is met
It is expressly provided for by the laws.
queries.answer: No; being expressly provided for by the laws is one of the conditions allowing processing without explicit consent.
queries.note: Casual/no diacritics. 'Expressly provided by laws' ground.

queries.text: Must all the conditions for processing without explicit consent be met together, or is one enough?
evidence: Personal data may be processed without seeking the explicit consent of the data subject only in cases where one of the following conditions is met
queries.answer: One is enough; processing without consent is possible where one of the conditions is met.
queries.note: Cumulative vs alternative conditions ('birinin').

queries.text: Are customers' fingerprint or facial recognition data special categories of personal data?
evidence: and the biometric and genetic data are deemed to be special categories of personal data
queries.answer: Yes; biometric data are special categories of personal data.
queries.note: Biometric data classification.

queries.text: Which category of data does information about an employee's criminal convictions fall into?
evidence: criminal convictions and security measures, and the biometric and genetic data are deemed to be special categories of personal data
queries.answer: Special categories of personal data.
queries.note: Criminal conviction data in HR context.

queries.text: What is the basic rule on processing special categories of personal data?
evidence: It is prohibited to process special categories of personal data.
queries.answer: Processing is prohibited, except under the listed conditions.
queries.note: Default prohibition after 2024 amendment.

queries.text: Who may process health data without consent for treatment and the financing of health-care services?
evidence: for the planning, management and financing of health-care services by persons subject to legal obligation of confidentiality or by competent public institutions and organizations
queries.answer: Persons subject to a legal obligation of confidentiality, or competent public institutions and organizations.
queries.note: Health-care ground restricted to persons under confidentiality obligation or competent institutions.

queries.text: Can an employee's health data be processed without explicit consent to meet occupational health and safety obligations?
evidence: It is necessary for the fulfilment of legal obligations in the fields of employment, occupational health and safety, social security, social services, and social assistance
queries.answer: Yes, where necessary to fulfil legal obligations in the field of occupational health and safety.
queries.note: Employment/OHS ground for special data.

queries.text: When processing special categories of data, whose measures must additionally be implemented?
evidence: Adequate measures, as determined by the Board, shall also be implemented in the processing of special categories of personal data.
queries.answer: Adequate measures determined by the Board.
queries.note: Adequate measures determined by the Board; distractor art. 8(2)(b) 'yeterli önlemler'.

queries.text: By which law, and of what date, was the paragraph setting the conditions for processing special categories of data amended?
evidence: (Amended: 2/3/2024- Art. 7499/33) It is prohibited to process special categories of personal data.
queries.note: Amendment metadata; answer is in a parenthetical annotation.

queries.text: May we freely process, for any purpose, health data the customer has made public himself/herself?
evidence: It relates to personal data that have been made public by the data subject, and processing is in consistent with data subject’s intention to make such data public
queries.answer: No; only where the processing is consistent with the data subject's intention to make the data public.
queries.note: Made-public special data needs consistency with intention; contrast with art. 5(2)(d).

queries.text: Can a trade union disclose its members' special category data to third parties under this exception?
evidence: is limited to the organizations’ fields of activity, and does not involve disclosure of data to third parties
queries.answer: No; the exception requires the processing to be limited to its field of activity and not disclosed to third parties.
queries.note: Non-profit/union ground: condition of non-disclosure to third parties.

queries.text: May we process special category data with the customer's explicit consent?
evidence: However, such processing is permitted under the following conditions: a) Data subject has given his/her explicit consent
queries.answer: Yes; the data subject's explicit consent is one of the conditions permitting processing of special categories of data.
queries.note: Casual/no diacritics. Explicit consent as ground for special data (post-2024 text).

queries.text: Which methods does the Law provide for personal data whose reasons for processing no longer exist?
evidence: personal data shall be erased, destructed or anonymized by the data controller, ex officio or on the request of the data subject, in the event that the reasons for the processing no longer exist
queries.answer: Erasure, destruction or anonymization.
queries.note: Three disposal methods; erasure by-law art. 7(1) restates it (conditioned on all art. 5/6 grounds ceasing).

queries.text: Can data that were processed lawfully still have to be erased?
evidence: Despite being processed in compliance with the provisions of this Law and other relevant laws
queries.answer: Yes; despite lawful processing, they must be erased, destroyed or anonymized once the reasons for processing no longer exist.
queries.note: Lawfully processed data still subject to erasure.

queries.text: According to the Law, by what type of instrument are the procedures for erasure, destruction and anonymization laid down?
evidence: Procedures and principles for the erasure, destruction or anonymization of personal data shall be laid down through by-law.
queries.answer: By a by-law (regulation).
queries.note: Delegation to a by-law; distractor: silme-md-03 cites art. 7(3) as its legal basis.

queries.text: If another law contains specific provisions on erasing data, do they remain valid alongside Article 7 of the KVKK?
evidence: The Provisions of other laws relating to the erasure, destruction or anonymization of personal data are reserved.
queries.answer: Yes; provisions of other laws on erasure, destruction or anonymization are reserved.
queries.note: Reservation of other laws.

queries.text: Must the data controller wait for the customer to ask before erasing the data?
evidence: by the data controller, ex officio or on the request of the data subject
queries.answer: No; the controller erases ex officio or on the data subject's request.
queries.note: Ex officio duty; controller must not wait for a request. Also in erasure by-law art. 7(1).

queries.text: What is the general rule for transferring customer data to another company?
evidence: Personal data shall not be transferred without explicit consent of the data subject.
queries.answer: Data shall not be transferred without the data subject's explicit consent (subject to the exceptions in art. 8(2)).
queries.note: Default rule for transfers; distractor art. 5(1) (processing).

queries.text: On the basis of the conditions listed in which provisions may data be transferred domestically without explicit consent?
evidence: a) the second paragraph of Article 5, b) the third paragraph of Article 6, provided that sufficient measures are taken.
queries.answer: One of the conditions in the second paragraph of Article 5, or (with sufficient measures) the third paragraph of Article 6.
queries.note: Cross-reference answer (art. 5(2) and art. 6(3)); answer is references, not substantive list.

queries.text: What additional condition applies when special category data are transferred without explicit consent?
evidence: the third paragraph of Article 6, provided that sufficient measures are taken
queries.answer: Sufficient measures must be taken.
queries.note: Extra condition for special-category transfers.

queries.text: Do special provisions on data transfer in other laws continue to apply alongside Article 8 of the KVKK?
evidence: The Provisions of other laws relating to transfer of personal data are reserved.
queries.answer: Yes; provisions of other laws relating to transfer of personal data are reserved.
queries.note: Reservation of other laws on transfer; distractor art. 9(10) for transfers abroad.

queries.text: Is explicit consent always required when transferring customer data to a group company?
evidence: Personal data may be transferred without seeking explicit consent of data subject upon the existence of one of the conditions provided for in
queries.answer: No; data may be transferred without explicit consent if one of the conditions of art. 5(2) (or art. 6(3), with sufficient measures) exists.
queries.note: Casual/no diacritics. Domestic transfer to group company; consent not always needed.

queries.text: If there is an adequacy decision for the destination country, is any other condition required for transfer abroad?
evidence: provided that one of the conditions set out in Article 5 and Article 6 is met and there is an adequacy decision
queries.answer: Yes; one of the conditions in Article 5 and Article 6 must also be met.
queries.note: Adequacy alone is not enough; needs art. 5/6 ground too. Mirrored in aktarim art. 6(1).

queries.text: Who issues the adequacy decision for transfers abroad and where is it published?
evidence: The adequacy decision shall be issued by the Board and published in the Official Gazette.
queries.answer: The Board issues it; it is published in the Official Gazette (per the by-law, also on the Authority's website).
queries.note: Issuer and publication; aktarim art. 8(4) adds publication on the Authority's website.

queries.text: At what maximum interval are adequacy decisions reassessed?
evidence: The adequacy decision shall be assessed at least every four years.
queries.answer: At least every four years.
queries.note: Numeric: every four years at the latest; also in aktarim art. 9(1).

queries.text: Can the Board revoke an adequacy decision with retroactive effect?
evidence: the Board may amend, suspend, or revoke the adequacy decision with prospective effect
queries.answer: No; it may amend, suspend or revoke it only with prospective effect.
queries.note: Prospective effect only; yes/no framing.

queries.text: Is reciprocity between Türkiye and the destination country taken into account when issuing an adequacy decision?
evidence: The reciprocity status concerning the transfer of personal data between Türkiye and the country
queries.answer: Yes; reciprocity concerning personal data transfers is among the elements primarily considered.
queries.note: One factor from a six-item list; aktarim art. 8(1) repeats the list.

queries.text: Without an adequacy decision, what condition regarding the data subject must be met in the destination country for a transfer under appropriate safeguards?
evidence: data subjects retain enforceable rights and effective legal remedies in the country to which the transfer is to be made
queries.answer: Data subjects must retain enforceable rights and effective legal remedies in that country.
queries.note: Condition attached to appropriate safeguards; mirrored in aktarim arts. 6(1)(b) and 10(1).

queries.text: Whose approval do binding corporate rules used for transfers abroad within a group of companies require?
evidence: The existence of binding corporate rules approved by the Board
queries.answer: The Board's approval.
queries.note: Binding corporate rules need Board approval; aktarim art. 12 details the application.

queries.text: Is a written commitment containing adequate protection provisions sufficient on its own for a transfer abroad?
evidence: The existence of a written commitment containing provisions to ensure adequate protection, and the Board’s approval for the transfer
queries.answer: No; the Board must also approve the transfer.
queries.note: Written undertaking needs Board permission too; contrast with standard contract (only notification).

queries.text: Within how many days must a standard contract signed for a transfer abroad be notified to the Authority?
evidence: The standard contract shall be notified to the Authority by the data controller or data processor within five business days following its signature.
queries.answer: Within five business days of its signature.
queries.note: Deadline: five business days. By-law counts from completion of signatures.

queries.text: Who is responsible for notifying the standard contract to the Authority?
evidence: The standard contract shall be notified to the Authority by the data controller or data processor within five business days following its signature.
If no such agreement is made, the data exporter shall be responsible for notifying the Board.
queries.answer: Under the Law, the data controller or data processor; under the by-law the parties may designate who, and failing that the data exporter notifies.
queries.note: Who notifies: Law says controller or processor; by-law lets parties designate, default is data exporter. Needs both to be complete.

queries.text: If there is neither an adequacy decision nor an appropriate safeguard, what character must a transfer abroad based on the exceptional cases have?
evidence: provided that such transfer is incidental
queries.answer: It must be incidental.
queries.note: 'Arızi' (incidental) condition; aktarim art. 16(1) defines incidental.

queries.text: When making an exceptional transfer abroad based on the customer's explicit consent, must the customer be informed of possible risks?
evidence: The data subject has given explicit consent to the transfer, provided that he/she has been informed of the potential risks involved
queries.answer: Yes; explicit consent must be given after being informed of the potential risks.
queries.note: Casual/no diacritics. Consent-based exceptional transfer requires risk information.

queries.text: In public-law activities of public institutions, which exceptional grounds for transfer abroad do not apply?
evidence: The provisions in subparagraphs (a), (b), and (c) of the sixth paragraph shall not apply to public law activities of public institutions and organizations.
queries.answer: Subparagraphs (a), (b) and (c) of the sixth paragraph (consent and contract-based grounds).
queries.note: Public-sector carve-out of (a)-(c); same in aktarim art. 16(4).

queries.text: What is required for a transfer abroad where the interests of Türkiye or the data subject would be seriously harmed?
evidence: only with the approval of the Board and after obtaining the opinion of the relevant public institution or organization
queries.answer: The Board's approval, after obtaining the opinion of the relevant public institution or organization.
queries.note: Serious-harm transfers need Board permission after public body opinion; also aktarim art. 6(3).

queries.text: Can data processors also transfer personal data abroad directly?
evidence: Personal data may be transferred abroad by data controllers and data processors
queries.answer: Yes; the Law allows transfers abroad by data controllers and data processors.
queries.note: Processors can transfer directly; answer is the actor list.

queries.text: At what point must the obligation to inform be fulfilled?
evidence: At the time when personal data are obtained
queries.answer: At the time when the personal data are obtained.
queries.note: Timing of the duty to inform.

queries.text: Apart from the data controller itself, who may carry out the informing?
evidence: the data controller or the person authorised by it is obliged to inform the data subjects
queries.answer: A person authorised by the data controller.
queries.note: Who informs: controller or its authorised person.

queries.text: Must the privacy notice state the legal basis for collecting the data?
evidence: the method and legal basis of collection of personal data
queries.answer: Yes; the method and legal basis of collection must be communicated.
queries.note: Content item: method and legal basis.

queries.text: When informing data subjects, must we also say to whom the data may be transferred?
evidence: to whom and for which purposes the processed personal data may be transferred
queries.answer: Yes; to whom and for which purposes the processed data may be transferred.
queries.note: Content item: recipients and purposes of transfer.

queries.text: Must the privacy notice also give the identity of the data controller's representative?
evidence: the identity of the data controller and of its representative, if any
queries.answer: Yes, the representative's identity must be given if there is one.
queries.note: Casual/no diacritics. Representative identity 'if any'.

queries.text: Which of their rights must data subjects be told about when being informed?
evidence: other rights referred to in Article 11
queries.answer: The rights referred to in Article 11.
queries.note: Rights reference to art. 11; answer is a cross-reference.

queries.text: Can a customer apply to the bank to find out whether personal data about him/her are being processed?
evidence: to learn whether his/her personal data are processed or not
queries.answer: Yes; he/she has the right to learn whether his/her personal data are processed.
queries.note: Right to learn whether data are processed.

queries.text: Does the data subject have the right to know which third parties abroad his/her data were transferred to?
evidence: to know the third parties to whom his personal data are transferred in country or abroad
queries.answer: Yes; the right to know the third parties to whom the data are transferred in the country or abroad.
queries.note: Right to know recipients, domestic or abroad.

queries.text: Can a customer ask for incomplete or incorrectly recorded information to be corrected?
evidence: to request the rectification of the incomplete or inaccurate data, if any
queries.answer: Yes; the right to request rectification of incomplete or inaccurate data.
queries.note: Rectification right.

queries.text: Can the data subject request that corrections or erasures be reported to the third parties the data were transferred to?
evidence: to request reporting of the operations carried out pursuant to sub-paragraphs (d) and (e) to third parties to whom his/her personal data have been transferred
queries.answer: Yes; he/she may request reporting of the operations under (d) and (e) to those third parties.
queries.note: Right (f): notification of corrections/erasures to recipients.

queries.text: If a fully automated credit-scoring system produces a result against a customer, what right does the customer have?
evidence: to object to the occurrence of a result against the person himself/herself by analyzing the data processed solely through automated systems
queries.answer: The right to object to a result against him/her arising from analysis solely through automated systems.
queries.note: Automated decision objection; scenario (credit scoring) paraphrased.

queries.text: Can a customer who suffered damage because his/her data were processed unlawfully claim compensation?
evidence: to claim compensation for the damage arising from the unlawful processing of his/her personal data
queries.answer: Yes; he/she has the right to claim compensation for the damage.
queries.note: Compensation right; distractor art. 14(3) general compensation for personal rights.

queries.text: Can a customer find out for what purpose his/her data are processed and whether they are used in line with that purpose?
evidence: to learn the purpose of the processing of his/her personal data and whether these personal data are used in compliance with the purpose
queries.answer: Yes; the right to learn the purpose of processing and whether data are used in compliance with it.
queries.note: Casual/no diacritics. Purpose and purpose-compatible use.

queries.text: The data subject's right to request erasure is subject to the conditions of which article?
evidence: to request the erasure or destruction of his/her personal data under the conditions referred to in Article 7
queries.answer: Article 7.
queries.note: Erasure right tied to art. 7; distractor silme-md-12.

queries.text: For what purposes must the data controller take technical and organizational measures?
evidence: preventing unlawful processing of personal data
preventing unlawful access to personal data
ensuring protection of personal data
queries.answer: To prevent unlawful processing, to prevent unlawful access, and to ensure protection of personal data.
queries.note: Three purposes of security measures; similar wording for processors abroad in aktarim art. 7 (different context).

queries.text: If data are processed by an external service provider, who is responsible for the security measures?
evidence: the data controller shall jointly be responsible with these persons for taking the measures laid down in the first paragraph
queries.answer: The data controller is jointly responsible with the person processing on its behalf.
queries.note: Joint liability with outsourced processors.

queries.text: Is the data controller obliged to carry out, or have carried out, KVKK compliance audits within its own organisation?
evidence: The data controller is obliged to carry out the necessary audits, or have them made, in its own institution or organization
queries.answer: Yes; it must carry out or have carried out the necessary audits.
queries.note: Internal audit duty; 'yapmak veya yaptırmak'.

queries.text: Does a data processor's obligation to keep learned personal data confidential continue after its role ends?
evidence: This obligation shall continue even after the end of their term of office.
queries.answer: Yes; the obligation continues even after the end of their term of office.
queries.note: Confidentiality survives end of role; distractor art. 23 has the same sentence for Board members/staff.

queries.text: May data controllers and processors use personal data they have learned for purposes other than the processing purpose?
evidence: shall not disclose the personal data that they have learned to anyone contrary to the provisions of this Law, neither shall they use such data for purposes other than that for which the personal data have been processed
queries.answer: No; they may not disclose them contrary to the Law or use them for other purposes.
queries.note: Purpose limitation duty of controllers/processors.

queries.text: If personal data are obtained by others through unlawful means, whom must the data controller notify?
evidence: the data controller shall communicate the breach to the data subject and notify it to the Board within the shortest time
queries.answer: The data subject and the Board.
queries.note: Breach notification addressees.

queries.text: Within how many hours must we notify the Board of a data breach?
evidence: the data controller shall communicate the breach to the data subject and notify it to the Board within the shortest time
queries.answer: The Law sets no number of hours; the breach must be notified to the data subject and the Board within the shortest time.
queries.note: Casual/no diacritics. Trap: the Law sets no hour count (no 72h rule anywhere in corpus); correct answer is 'en kısa sürede'.

queries.text: Can the Board announce a data breach publicly?
evidence: Where necessary, the Board may announce such breach at its official website or through in any other way it deems appropriate.
queries.answer: Yes; where necessary, on its website or by any other method it deems appropriate.
queries.note: Board may publicise breach.

queries.text: Is it enough to take only technical measures for data security?
evidence: to take all necessary technical and organizational measures to provide an appropriate level of security
queries.answer: No; all necessary technical and organizational measures must be taken for an appropriate level of security.
queries.note: Measures must be technical AND administrative/organizational.

queries.text: How long was given to bring personal data processed before the Law's publication into compliance?
evidence: The personal data that were processed before the publication date of this Law shall be rendered compatible with the provisions of this Law within two years as of its date of publication.
queries.answer: Two years from the date of publication.
queries.note: Numeric transitional deadline: two years.

queries.text: Were consents lawfully obtained before the Law deemed valid afterwards?
evidence: consents duly taken before the publication date of this Law shall be deemed compatible with the provisions of this Law, unless no declaration of intent is made to the contrary within one year
queries.answer: Yes; they are deemed compatible unless a contrary declaration of intent is made within one year.
queries.note: Legacy consents; one-year window (note: EN wording has a double negative).

queries.text: During the transition, when had legacy data found to be non-compliant with the Law to be erased?
evidence: The personal data which are found to be not complying with the provisions of this Law shall be immediately erased, destructed or anonymized.
queries.answer: Immediately (erased, destroyed or anonymized).
queries.note: 'Derhal' — immediacy for non-compliant legacy data.

queries.text: Under the transitional provisions, who sets the deadline for data controllers to register with the Data Controllers' Registry?
evidence: Data controllers are obliged to register with the Data Controllers’ Registry within the time specified and announced by the Board.
queries.answer: The Board; registration must be made within the time specified and announced by the Board.
queries.note: Registry deadline set by Board; distractors art. 16 and sicil-md-08 (before starting processing / 30 days).

queries.text: Within what period were the by-laws provided for by the Law to be brought into force?
evidence: The by-laws provided for by this Law shall be brought into force within one year as of the date of publication of this Law.
queries.answer: Within one year of the Law's publication.
queries.note: By-laws deadline one year; distractor art. 31 (who issues by-laws).

queries.text: What were public institutions required to do during the transition to coordinate implementation of the Law?
evidence: A high-level executive, to ensure coordination with regard to the implementation of the Law in public institutions and organisations, shall be appointed and notified to the Presidency within one year
queries.answer: Appoint a high-level executive and notify the Presidency within one year.
queries.note: Public-sector coordination officer.

queries.text: Which of the first-elected Board members serve six years, and how long do the others serve?
evidence: The term of office for the first elected President, the Second President, and two members who are determined by ballot, shall be six years; this period shall be four years for the remaining five members.
queries.answer: The President, the Second President and two members chosen by ballot serve six years; the other five serve four years.
queries.note: First Board terms (6 vs 4 years); distractor art. 21 general term of office.

queries.text: Until the Authority was allocated a budget, where were its expenses covered from?
evidence: The expenditures of the Authority shall be reimbursed by the budget of the office of the Prime Minister.
queries.answer: From the budget of the office of the Prime Minister.
queries.note: Interim funding source.

queries.text: Under Provisional Article 2, at most how many people can be appointed as Personal Data Protection Experts?
evidence: Number of personnel to be assigned in regard may not exceed fifteen.
queries.answer: Fifteen.
queries.note: Numeric cap; distractor art. 26 (experts in general).

queries.text: What minimum foreign language exam score is required to be appointed as an expert under this provisional article?
evidence: having taken minimum 70 points at Foreign Language Placement Test
queries.answer: At least 70 points.
queries.note: Language score threshold.

queries.text: Is there an age limit for being appointed as an expert under Provisional Article 2?
evidence: who are younger than 40 year old may be assigned as Personal Data Protection Expert
queries.answer: Yes; the person must be younger than 40.
queries.note: Casual/no diacritics. Age limit; EN omits 'as of appointment date'.

queries.text: Until what date did the pre-amendment first paragraph of Article 9 continue to apply?
evidence: The first paragraph of Article 9, as it existed before the amendment introduced by the law, shall remain in effect until 1/9/2024
queries.note: Date: old art. 9(1) applied until 1/9/2024.

queries.text: What happens to applications pending before the criminal judgeships of peace as of 1/6/2024?
evidence: Applications pending before the criminal judgeships of peace as of 1/6/2024 shall continue to be processed by these judgeships.
queries.answer: They continue to be handled by those judgeships.
queries.note: Pending applications before criminal judgeships of peace.

queries.text: After the 2024 amendment, were the old and new versions of Article 9 on transfers abroad applied side by side for a while?
evidence: shall remain in effect until 1/9/2024, alongside the amended version that entered into force
queries.answer: Yes; the old first paragraph remained in effect alongside the amended version until 1/9/2024.
queries.note: Yes/no: old and new art. 9 ran in parallel during transition.

queries.text: If a customer asks for incompletely recorded information to be corrected, within how many days must the bank conclude the request, and may it charge a fee?
evidence: to request the rectification of the incomplete or inaccurate data, if any
at the latest within thirty days and free of charge. However if the action requires an extra cost, fees may be charged in the tariff determined by the Board.
queries.answer: Rectification is a right under art. 11; it must be concluded within thirty days at the latest, free of charge as a rule (a fee per the Board's tariff may be charged if extra cost arises).
queries.note: Needs right to rectification (art. 11) + response deadline and fee rule (art. 13).

queries.text: A company that does not tell customers for what purpose their data will be processed when collecting them breaches which obligation, and what administrative fine does it face?
evidence: the purpose of processing of personal data
An administrative fine of 5.000 to 100.000 TL shall be imposed on those who fail to fulfil the obligation to inform as stipulated in Article 10
queries.answer: It breaches the obligation to inform under Article 10; the fine is 5,000 to 100,000 TL.
queries.note: Needs art. 10 (purpose must be disclosed) + art. 18(1)(a) fine range.

queries.text: What range of administrative fine applies to a data controller that fails to take measures to prevent unauthorised access to data?
evidence: preventing unlawful access to personal data
An administrative fine of 15.000 to 1.000.000 TL shall be imposed on those who fail to fulfil the obligations related to data security as stipulated in Article 12
queries.answer: As a breach of the data security obligations in Article 12, 15,000 to 1,000,000 TL.
queries.note: Needs art. 12 (duty to prevent unlawful access) + art. 18(1)(b) fine range.

queries.text: Can a data processor that fails to notify a standard contract to the Authority in time be fined; what are the notification deadline and the fine range?
evidence: The standard contract shall be notified to the Authority by the data controller or data processor within five business days following its signature.
An administrative fine of 50.000 to 1.000.000 TL shall be imposed on those who fail to fulfil the obligation to notify as stipulated in Article 9(5).
the fine stipulated in subparagraph (d) shall be imposed on the data controller or on natural persons and legal persons governed by private law that process data
after finalisation of the signatures, shall be notified to the Authority within five business days
queries.answer: Yes; notification is due within five business days of signature, otherwise a fine of 50,000 to 1,000,000 TL applies to the controller or processor.
queries.note: Needs art. 9(5) deadline + art. 18(1)(d) fine and 18(2) on who can be fined (processors too). By-law art. 14(5) restates the 5-business-day deadline (from completion of signatures).

queries.text: A bank with a data retention and disposal policy must erase data whose processing reasons have ceased by when at the latest?
evidence: personal data shall be erased, destructed or anonymized by the data controller, ex officio or on the request of the data subject, in the event that the reasons for the processing no longer exist
in the first periodic disposal process following the date when obligation of erasure, destruction or anonymization of personal data arises
This time interval cannot exceed six months in any case.
queries.answer: In the first periodic disposal after the obligation arises; the periodic disposal interval can never exceed six months.
queries.note: Law gives the duty (art. 7), by-law gives the timing (first periodic disposal, max 6 months).

queries.text: Under which provision is a person criminally liable for failing to erase or anonymize data after the reasons for processing have ceased?
evidence: personal data shall be erased, destructed or anonymized by the data controller, ex officio or on the request of the data subject, in the event that the reasons for the processing no longer exist
Those who do not erase or anonymize personal data as contrary to the provision of Article 7 of this Law shall be punished in accordance with Article 138 of the Law No. 5237.
queries.answer: It breaches Article 7 and is punished under Article 138 of the Turkish Penal Code No. 5237.
queries.note: Duty in art. 7 + criminal sanction in art. 17(2) (Turkish Penal Code art. 138).

queries.text: When a customer requests erasure of his/her data and all processing conditions have ceased, by when must the data controller conclude the request?
evidence: to request the erasure or destruction of his/her personal data under the conditions referred to in Article 7
The data controller shall act on the request of the data subject at the latest within thirty days and inform the data subject.
queries.answer: Erasure is a right under Article 11; the controller erases/destroys/anonymizes the data and concludes the request within thirty days at the latest, informing the data subject.
queries.note: Right to erasure (art. 11(e)) + by-law deadline for requests (30 days, inform data subject).

queries.text: A customer asked to know the third parties his/her data were transferred to and was refused; within what period can he/she complain to the Board?
evidence: to know the third parties to whom his personal data are transferred in country or abroad
within thirty days as of he or she learns about the response of the data controller, or within sixty days as of the request date, in any case
queries.answer: This is a right under Article 11; a complaint can be lodged within thirty days of learning of the refusal, and in any case within sixty days of the request date.
queries.note: Right to know recipients (art. 11(ç)) + complaint windows (art. 14(1)): 30 days from learning / 60 days from application.

queries.text: When data are processed to prevent crime, which of the data subject's Article 11 rights survives the exemption?
evidence: Article 11 regarding the rights of the data subject, excluding the right to claim compensation
is necessary for the prevention of committing a crime or for crime investigation.
to claim compensation for the damage arising from the unlawful processing of his/her personal data
queries.answer: The right to claim compensation for damage arising from unlawful processing.
queries.note: Art. 28(2) suspends arts. 10, 11 and 16 for crime-prevention processing except the compensation right in art. 11(ğ).

queries.text: Can an employer transfer an employee's health data to a third party without explicit consent to meet occupational health and safety obligations, and under what additional condition?
evidence: It is necessary for the fulfilment of legal obligations in the fields of employment, occupational health and safety, social security, social services, and social assistance
the third paragraph of Article 6, provided that sufficient measures are taken
queries.answer: Yes; where necessary for legal obligations in occupational health and safety (art. 6(3)), provided that sufficient measures are taken.
queries.note: Special-category ground (art. 6(3)(f)) + transfer rule requiring sufficient measures (art. 8(2)(b)).

queries.text: When a customer submits a request under the data protection law to the bank, within how many days at the latest must we conclude it?
evidence: within the shortest time by taking into account the nature of the demand and at the latest within thirty days and free of charge
queries.answer: As soon as possible given the nature of the request, and within thirty days at the latest.
queries.note: Deadline number; silme-md-12 repeats 30 days for erasure requests only (consistent).

queries.text: By which means can a data subject submit a request to the data controller?
evidence: to the data controller in writing or by other means to be determined by the Board
queries.answer: In writing or by other means to be determined by the Board.
queries.note: Channels of application; easy.

queries.text: Can we charge a fee when answering a data subject's request?
evidence: However if the action requires an extra cost, fees may be charged in the tariff determined by the Board.
queries.answer: In principle it is free of charge; but if the action requires an extra cost, a fee under the tariff determined by the Board may be charged.
queries.note: Casual TR without diacritics; fee exception.

queries.text: If we refuse a request, do we have to state the reasons for the refusal?
evidence: The data controller shall act on the request or refuse it together with justified grounds
queries.answer: Yes; the data controller may refuse the request only together with justified grounds.
queries.note: Yes/no on justification for refusal.

queries.text: In what form must we communicate our response to the data subject's request?
evidence: communicate its response to the data subject in writing or by electronic means
queries.answer: In writing or by electronic means.
queries.note: Form of the response.

queries.text: We charged a customer a fee for a request, but the request arose from our own fault. What happens to the fee?
evidence: If the request is made due to fault of the data controller, the fee is refunded to data subject.
queries.answer: The fee is refunded to the data subject.
queries.note: Refund condition; what-happens-if form.

queries.text: Once we accept the demand in a request, who is obliged to carry it out?
evidence: In case the demand in the request is accepted, it shall be fulfilled by the data controller.
queries.answer: The data controller.
queries.note: Obligation after accepting; answer is short and a bit generic.

queries.text: A customer whose request was refused: within how many days after learning our response can they complain to the Board?
evidence: within thirty days as of he or she learns about the response of the data controller
queries.answer: Within thirty days of learning the response (and in any case within sixty days of the request date).
queries.note: 30-day complaint window counted from learning the response; two deadlines in same sentence.

queries.text: For a person who never received an answer to their request to the bank, when at the latest, counted from the request date, does the time to complain to the Board run out?
evidence: or within sixty days as of the request date, in any case
queries.answer: Within sixty days from the request date.
queries.note: Outer 60-day limit from request date; distractor is the 30-day limit.

queries.text: Can a customer complain directly to the Personal Data Protection Board without first applying to us?
evidence: A complaint shall not be lodged before exhausting the remedy of the request to the data controller pursuant to Article 13.
queries.answer: No; a complaint cannot be lodged before exhausting the request to the data controller.
queries.note: Yes/no: exhaustion of the controller remedy.

queries.text: In which situations can a data subject lodge a complaint with the Board?
evidence: If the request is refused, the response is found insufficient or the request is not responded within the specified time period
queries.answer: When the request is refused, the response is found insufficient, or the request is not answered in time.
queries.note: Casual TR; list of three triggers.

queries.text: Does the KVKK complaint procedure remove the right of a customer whose personal rights were violated to claim compensation under the general provisions?
evidence: The right to compensation, under the general provisions, of those whose personal rights are violated, is reserved.
queries.answer: No; the right to compensation under the general provisions is reserved.
queries.note: Compensation reserved; 11(ğ) is a related but different right.

queries.text: The Board has asked us for information and documents as part of an examination. Within how many days must we send them?
evidence: shall send the information and documents demanded by the Board related to the subject of examination within fifteen days
queries.answer: Within fifteen days.
queries.note: Casual TR; crisp number (15 days) for document requests.

queries.text: Is there any category of documents excepted from the duty to send the Board the information and documents it requests during an examination?
evidence: Except for the information and documents having the status of state secret
queries.answer: Yes; information and documents having the status of state secret are excepted.
queries.note: Exception to disclosure duty.

queries.text: If the Board wants to carry out an on-site inspection at our company, are we obliged to allow it?
evidence: shall enable, where necessary, on-the-spot examination
queries.answer: Yes; the data controller must enable on-the-spot examination where necessary.
queries.note: Yes/no on on-site inspection.

queries.text: If the Board never answers a complaint, after how many days from the complaint date is the demand deemed refused?
evidence: In case it is not responded in sixty days from the date of complaint the demand shall be deemed refused.
queries.answer: Sixty days.
queries.note: Deemed-refusal rule; 60 days also appears in art. 14 in a different sense.

queries.text: When the Board decides that an infringement it found must be remedied and notifies us, how long do we have to implement the decision?
evidence: This decision shall be implemented without delay and within thirty days at the latest after the notification
queries.answer: Without delay and within thirty days at the latest after notification.
queries.note: Deadline to implement a Board remedy decision.

queries.text: In what case does the Board adopt and publish a resolution on the matter (a principle decision)?
evidence: in cases where it is determined that the infringement is widespread, the Board shall take a resolution on this matter and publishes this resolution
queries.answer: When the examination determines that the infringement is widespread.
queries.note: Condition for a published principle decision (ilke kararı).

queries.text: Under what conditions may the Board decide to stop data processing or the transfer of data abroad?
evidence: The Board may decide to stop the processing of personal data or transfer of personal data abroad in the case damages which are difficult or impossible to compensate for, and in the event of explicit infringement of the law.
queries.answer: Where damages difficult or impossible to compensate arise and there is an explicit infringement of the law.
queries.note: Two cumulative conditions for stopping processing/transfer; 22(c) mentions temporary measures only generally.

queries.text: Will the Board examine a notice or complaint that does not meet the conditions of the law on the right to petition?
evidence: The notices and complaints not meeting conditions pursuant to Article 6 of the Law No. 3071 of 1/11/1984 on the Use of Right to Petition shall not be examined.
queries.answer: No, it will not be examined.
queries.note: Paraphrased reference to the Right to Petition Law.

queries.text: Can the Board start an examination even without receiving a complaint?
evidence: The Board shall carry out the necessary examination on the matters falling within its task upon complaint or ex officio where it has learnt about the alleged infringement.
queries.answer: Yes; it examines ex officio where it learns about an alleged infringement.
queries.note: Ex officio examination; 22(c) says the same in a list, consistent.

queries.text: Is it enough to register with the Data Controllers' Registry after we have started processing data?
evidence: Natural or legal persons who process personal data shall register with the Data Controllers’ Registry prior to the start of data processing.
queries.answer: No; registration must be made before the start of data processing.
queries.note: Registration timing; sicil-md-08(1) says the same (listed).

queries.text: Who has the power to grant an exemption from the obligation to register with the Registry?
evidence: the Board may provide derogation from the obligation of registration with the Data Controllers’ Registry
queries.answer: The Personal Data Protection Board.
queries.note: Who may grant a registration exemption; sicil-md-16 lists fuller criteria (listed).

queries.text: Must the registration notification include the personal data planned to be transferred abroad?
evidence: The personal data which are envisaged to be transferred abroad
queries.answer: Yes; the personal data envisaged to be transferred abroad are part of the notification.
queries.note: Content of the registration notification; sicil-md-09(1)(d) repeats it (listed).

queries.text: By what type of instrument are the detailed procedures and principles of the Registry laid down?
evidence: Other procedures and principles relating to the Data Controllers’ Registry shall be laid down through a by-law.
queries.answer: By a by-law (regulation).
queries.note: Delegation to secondary legislation; low lexical overlap.

queries.text: Which provisions of which law apply to crimes concerning personal data?
evidence: Articles 135 to 140 of Turkish Penal Code No. 5237 of 26/9/2004 shall be applied to the crimes concerning personal data.
queries.answer: Articles 135 to 140 of Turkish Penal Code No. 5237.
queries.note: Cross-reference to the Penal Code article range.

queries.text: Under which article of the Turkish Penal Code are those who fail to erase or anonymise data that should be erased punished?
evidence: Those who do not erase or anonymize personal data as contrary to the provision of Article 7 of this Law shall be punished in accordance with Article 138 of the Law No. 5237.
queries.answer: Under Article 138 of Law No. 5237 (the Penal Code).
queries.note: Casual TR; specific TCK article number (138).

queries.text: What administrative fine range does the Law provide for a data controller that fails to fulfil the obligation to inform?
evidence: An administrative fine of 5.000 to 100.000 TL shall be imposed on those who fail to fulfil the obligation to inform as stipulated in Article 10
queries.note: Fine range for information-obligation breach; amounts as stated in text.

queries.text: What are the minimum and maximum administrative fines for failing to comply with data security obligations?
evidence: An administrative fine of 15.000 to 1.000.000 TL shall be imposed on those who fail to fulfil the obligations related to data security as stipulated in Article 12
queries.answer: Between 15,000 TL and 1,000,000 TL.
queries.note: Fine range for data security failures.

queries.text: How large an administrative fine can be imposed on a data controller that fails to comply with a Board decision?
evidence: An administrative fine of 25.000 to 1.000.000 TL shall be imposed on those who fail to comply with the decisions issued by the Board as stipulated in Article 15
queries.note: Fine for non-compliance with Board decisions.

queries.text: How much is the administrative fine for a company that does not register with the Data Controllers' Registry (VERBIS)?
evidence: An administrative fine of 20.000 to 1.000.000 TL shall be imposed on those who act contrary to the obligations for registry with the Data Controllers’ Registry and for notification as stipulated in Article 16
queries.note: Casual TR; registry fine. sicil-md-17 only refers to 18(1)(ç) without amounts.

queries.text: What is the administrative fine for failing to fulfil the notification obligation in Article 9(5) on transfers abroad?
evidence: An administrative fine of 50.000 to 1.000.000 TL shall be imposed on those who fail to fulfil the obligation to notify as stipulated in Article 9(5).
queries.note: 2024 amendment: fine for the standard-contract notification duty in 9(5).

queries.text: As a company acting as a data processor, can we also be given an administrative fine under the KVKK?
evidence: the fine stipulated in subparagraph (d) shall be imposed on the data controller or on natural persons and legal persons governed by private law that process data
queries.answer: Only the fine under subparagraph (d) (the Article 9(5) notification duty) can also be imposed on data processors that are natural persons or private-law legal persons; the other fines are imposed on the data controller.
queries.note: Who is fined; requires reading the 2024 amended para. 2.

queries.text: On whom are the administrative fines for breaches of the information, data security, Board-decision and registry obligations imposed?
evidence: The administrative fines provided for in subparagraphs (a), (b), (c) and (ç) of the first paragraph shall be imposed on the data controller
queries.answer: On the data controller.
queries.note: Addressee of fines (a)-(ç).

queries.text: In which courts can an action be brought against an administrative fine imposed by the Board?
evidence: Administrative fines imposed by the Board may be appealed in administrative courts.
queries.answer: In administrative courts.
queries.note: Competent court for appeals against fines.

queries.text: If a breach of the information or data security obligations occurs within a public institution, what happens to the civil servants responsible?
evidence: the disciplinary provisions shall be applied to the civil servants and other public officers employed in the relevant public institutions and organizations
queries.answer: Upon notice of the Board, disciplinary provisions are applied and the result is reported to the Board.
queries.note: Public-sector consequence: disciplinary action instead; sicil-md-17(2) repeats it for registry only.

queries.text: What is the legal status of the Personal Data Protection Authority; is it autonomous?
evidence: Personal Data Protection Authority, which is a public legal entity and has administrative and financial autonomy
queries.answer: It is a public legal entity with administrative and financial autonomy.
queries.note: Legal status of the Authority.

queries.text: Which office is the Data Protection Authority affiliated with?
evidence: The Authority is affiliated to the Minister assigned by the President of the Republic.
queries.answer: The Minister assigned by the President of the Republic.
queries.note: Affiliation; short answer.

queries.text: In which city is the Data Protection Authority headquartered?
evidence: The Headquarters of the Authority is in Ankara
queries.answer: Ankara.
queries.note: Casual TR; headquarters.

queries.text: What bodies make up the Authority, and which one is its decision-making body?
evidence: The Authority is composed of the Board and the Presidency. Decision making body of the Authority is the Board.
queries.answer: It is composed of the Board and the Presidency; the Board is the decision-making body.
queries.note: Organs of the Authority and its decision body.

queries.text: To whom is the Authority's annual activity report submitted?
evidence: to transmit the annual activity report to the Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye, the Committee on Human Rights Inquiry of Grand National Assembly of Türkiye
queries.answer: To the Presidency of the Republic and the Human Rights Inquiry Committee of the Grand National Assembly.
queries.note: Recipients of the annual report.

queries.text: Can the Authority cooperate with universities or NGOs on matters within its field of duty?
evidence: to cooperate with public institutions and organisations, non-governmental organizations, professional associations or universities within its field of duty, if needed
queries.answer: Yes; where needed it cooperates with public institutions, NGOs, professional associations or universities.
queries.note: Domestic cooperation partners listed.

queries.text: Do the Authority's duties include cooperating with international organisations and attending meetings?
evidence: within its field of duty cooperate with international organisations and participate in the meetings
queries.answer: Yes; it follows international developments, cooperates with international organisations and participates in meetings.
queries.note: International dimension of Authority duties.

queries.text: How many members does the Personal Data Protection Board have and who elects them?
evidence: The Board consists of nine members. Five members of the Board shall be elected by the Grand National Assembly of Türkiye; four members shall be elected by the President of the Republic of Türkiye.
queries.answer: Nine members; five elected by the Grand National Assembly and four by the President.
queries.note: Board size and appointing bodies.

queries.text: Can a member of a political party become a Board member?
evidence: Not being a member of any political party.
queries.answer: No; not being a member of any political party is a requirement.
queries.note: Eligibility: political party membership.

queries.text: What minimum level of education is required for Board membership?
evidence: Having a bachelor degree of at least four years.
queries.answer: A bachelor degree of at least four years.
queries.note: Eligibility: minimum education.

queries.text: Before whom do newly elected Board members take their oath?
evidence: Members of the Board shall take the following oath before the First Presidency Board of the Court of Cassation
queries.answer: Before the First Presidency Board of the Court of Cassation.
queries.note: Oath venue.

queries.text: May Board members act as arbitrators or expert witnesses while in office?
evidence: shall not act as arbitrators and expert witnesses
queries.answer: No, unless provided for by a specific law they may not act as arbitrators or expert witnesses.
queries.note: Incompatibilities: arbitration / expert witness.

queries.text: Can Board members give lectures and receive conference fees?
evidence: Board members may prepare scientific publications, give lectures and attend conferences provided that these will not hinder their primary duties
queries.answer: Yes; provided it does not hinder their primary duties, they may lecture, attend conferences and receive the associated fees.
queries.note: Exception to incompatibilities: teaching/publishing.

queries.text: After what periods of unexcused absence from work does a Board member's membership end?
evidence: it is ascertained that they have been absent from work for fifteen consecutive days or for a total of thirty days within a year, without legitimate permission and excuse
queries.answer: Fifteen consecutive days, or a total of thirty days within a year.
queries.note: Removal for absence: two thresholds.

queries.text: In what case does the membership of a Board member who skips Board meetings without excuse end?
evidence: it is ascertained that they fail to attend three Board meetings in one month and ten Board meetings in one year without any permission and excuse
queries.answer: If they miss three Board meetings in one month or ten in one year without permission or excuse.
queries.note: Removal for missed meetings; numbers 3 and 10.

queries.text: Who grants permission to investigate Board members for crimes allegedly committed in connection with their duties?
evidence: permission for investigation shall be granted by the President of Türkiye
queries.answer: The President of Türkiye.
queries.note: Investigation permission for duty-related crimes.

queries.text: Within how many days after announcing the candidates does the Grand National Assembly hold the election of Board members?
evidence: The election of the members of the Board shall be made within ten days after the nomination and announcement of the candidates.
queries.answer: Within ten days after the nomination and announcement of the candidates.
queries.note: Parliamentary election timing (10 days).

queries.text: Which body decides on the complaints of people who claim their personal data rights were violated?
evidence: to conclude the complaints of those who claim that their rights with regard to personal data protection have been violated.
queries.answer: The Personal Data Protection Board.
queries.note: Board decides complaints.

queries.text: Who determines the adequate measures required for processing special categories of personal data (e.g. health data)?
evidence: to determine the adequate measures which are necessary for the processing of special categories of personal data.
queries.answer: The Board.
queries.note: Who sets adequate measures for special categories; art. 6 not in slice.

queries.text: Which body decides on the administrative sanctions provided for in the KVKK?
evidence: to decide on the imposition of administrative sanctions provided for in this Law.
queries.answer: The Board.
queries.note: Casual TR; who decides sanctions.

queries.text: Does the Board give an opinion on draft legislation prepared by another institution that contains personal data provisions?
evidence: to deliver its opinion about draft legislation prepared by other institutions or organizations that contain provisions on personal data.
queries.answer: Yes; delivering an opinion on such drafts is one of the Board's duties.
queries.note: Advisory role on draft legislation.

queries.text: Who has the power to issue regulatory acts determining data security obligations?
evidence: to carry out regulatory act to determine obligations related to data security
queries.answer: The Board.
queries.note: Regulatory power on data security obligations.

queries.text: What is the minimum number of members for the Board to convene?
evidence: The Board shall convene at least with six members, including the President
queries.answer: At least six members, including the President.
queries.note: Meeting quorum.

queries.text: Who has the power to call the Board to an extraordinary meeting?
evidence: The President may summon the Board for an extraordinary meeting, if necessary.
queries.answer: The President.
queries.note: Extraordinary meeting power.

queries.text: By what majority does the Board take decisions?
evidence: shall take decisions by simple majority of its total members
queries.answer: By simple (absolute) majority of its total members.
queries.note: Decision majority: of total membership, not of those present.

queries.text: Can Board members abstain in a vote?
evidence: Members of the Board shall not cast abstaining vote.
queries.answer: No, they cannot cast abstaining votes.
queries.note: Casual TR; yes/no on abstention.

queries.text: A Board member may not attend meetings or vote on matters concerning relatives up to which degree?
evidence: their relatives by blood up to third degree and relatives by affinity of marriage up to second degree
queries.answer: Blood relatives up to third degree and relatives by marriage up to second degree (also adopted children and spouses, even former).
queries.note: Recusal: degree of kinship.

queries.text: Within what period after the decision date must Board decisions and any dissenting reasons be written?
evidence: The decisions and the grounds for the counter vote, if any, shall be written within 15 days at the latest.
queries.answer: Within fifteen days at the latest.
queries.note: Deadline to write decisions (15 days).

queries.text: Are deliberations at Board meetings open to the public?
evidence: Unless otherwise agreed, debates at the Board meetings are confidential.
queries.answer: No; unless otherwise agreed, they are confidential.
queries.note: Confidentiality of deliberations.

queries.text: Does Board members' duty to keep secrets learned during their work continue after they leave office?
evidence: This obligation shall continue even after the end of their term of office.
queries.answer: Yes, it continues after the end of their term of office.
queries.note: Secrecy survives term; similar sentence exists in art. 12(4) for controllers, different subject.

queries.text: Who acts on behalf of the President of the Authority in his or her absence?
evidence: The Second President is entitled to act on behalf of the President in his/her absence.
queries.answer: The Second President.
queries.note: Deputy in absence of the President.

queries.text: Who appoints the Authority's Vice President and heads of departments?
evidence: to appoint Vice President, Heads of Departments and Authority’s personnel.
queries.answer: The President of the Authority.
queries.note: Appointment power.

queries.text: Whose duty is it to prepare the Authority's annual budget and financial tables?
evidence: to prepare the annual budget and financial tables of the Authority in line with the determined strategies, annual purposes and objectives.
queries.answer: The President's.
queries.note: Budget preparation duty.

queries.text: What is the maximum number of departments within the Presidency?
evidence: The number of departments shall not be more than seven.
queries.answer: Seven; the number of departments cannot exceed seven.
queries.note: Casual TR; cap on departments.

queries.text: What qualifications are required to be appointed as Vice President or head of department?
evidence: among those who have a bachelor degree of at least 4 year program and served in the public institutions for at least ten years
queries.answer: A bachelor degree of at least four years and at least ten years of public service.
queries.note: Qualifications: 4-year degree and 10 years public service.

queries.text: Who represents the Authority, and how, in lawsuits to which it is a party?
evidence: to represent the Authority through attorneys-at-law at the proceedings and enforcement proceedings to which the Authority is a party
queries.answer: The Presidency, through attorneys-at-law.
queries.note: Litigation representation.

queries.text: Who brings into force the by-law that sets out the Authority's service units and their working principles?
evidence: shall be laid down through a by-law which is brought into force by President of the Republic of Türkiye
queries.answer: The President of the Republic, upon the Authority's proposal.
queries.note: Service-unit by-law issued by the President of the Republic (contrast art. 31).

queries.text: Is there a career benefit for those appointed as Personal Data Protection Experts?
evidence: shall receive one extra grade for once only
queries.answer: Yes; they receive one extra grade, once only.
queries.note: Only substantive content of art. 26.

queries.text: What are the limits on the number and duration of public personnel temporarily seconded to the Authority?
evidence: shall not exceed ten per cent of the total number of posts for Personal Data Protection Experts and Personal Data Protection Assistant Experts, and the term of assignment shall not exceed two years.
queries.answer: Not more than ten per cent of the total expert and assistant expert posts; not more than two years (extendable in one-year periods if needed).
queries.note: Secondment cap and duration; two numbers.

queries.text: Which law governs the Authority's personnel on matters not regulated by the KVKK?
evidence: Personnel of the Authority shall be subject to the Law No. 657, excluding the matters regulated through this Law.
queries.answer: Law No. 657 (Civil Servants Law).
queries.note: Governing personnel law.

queries.text: Whose consent is needed to second a judge or public prosecutor temporarily to the Authority?
evidence: judges and public prosecutors may be seconded upon their consent
queries.answer: The judge's or prosecutor's own consent.
queries.note: Consent requirement differs for judges/prosecutors.

queries.text: Is a person's processing of data purely for activities concerning themselves and family members living in the same home covered by the KVKK?
evidence: processed by natural persons within the scope of purely personal activities of the data subject or of family members living together with him/her in the same dwelling provided that it is not to be disclosed to third parties and the obligations about data security is to be complied with
queries.answer: No; the Law does not apply, provided the data is not disclosed to third parties and data security obligations are complied with.
queries.note: Household exemption with conditions.

queries.text: On what condition is processing for official statistics exempt from the KVKK?
evidence: personal data are processed for official statistics and provided that they are being anonymized for the purposes for such as research, planning and statistics.
queries.answer: Provided the data are anonymised (for purposes such as research, planning and statistics).
queries.note: Statistics exemption requires anonymisation.

queries.text: Is personal data processing by courts in the course of proceedings subject to the KVKK?
evidence: personal data are processed by judicial authorities or execution authorities with regard to investigation, prosecution, judicial or execution proceedings.
queries.answer: No; the Law does not apply to processing by judicial or execution authorities for investigation, prosecution, judicial or execution proceedings.
queries.note: Judicial authorities exemption.

queries.text: Does the obligation to inform apply when processing data that the customer made public themselves?
evidence: Article 10 regarding the data controller's obligation to inform
is carried out on the data which are made public by the data subject himself/herself.
queries.answer: No; provided it is compliant and proportionate with the Law's purpose and principles, Article 10 (obligation to inform) does not apply.
