queries.note: Partial exemption: data made public by data subject -> art. 10 not applied. sicil-md-15 covers only registry.

queries.text: Which KVKK articles do not apply to processing necessary for a crime investigation?
evidence: Article 10 regarding the data controller's obligation to inform, Article 11 regarding the rights of the data subject, excluding the right to claim compensation, and Article 16 regarding the obligation to register with the Data Controllers’ Registry shall not be applied
queries.answer: Article 10 (obligation to inform), Article 11 (data subject rights, except the right to claim compensation) and Article 16 (registry obligation).
queries.note: Which articles are disapplied in partial-exemption cases.

queries.text: Is processing data for artistic or scientific purposes or within freedom of expression exempt from the KVKK?
evidence: within the scope of freedom of expression provided that national defence, national security, public security, public order, economic security, right to privacy or personal rights are not violated or the process doesn’t constitute a crime.
queries.answer: Yes, provided that national defence, national security, public security, public order, economic security, privacy or personal rights are not violated and it does not constitute a crime.
queries.note: Casual TR; freedom of expression exemption and its limits.

queries.text: Can the Authority accept donations; are donations among its revenues?
evidence: Donations and grants received.
queries.answer: Yes; donations and grants received are among the Authority's revenues.
queries.note: Revenue list; donations.

queries.text: Under the procedures of which law is the Authority's budget prepared?
evidence: The budget of the Authority shall be prepared and adopted in accordance with procedures and principles provided for in the Law No. 5018.
queries.answer: Law No. 5018 (Public Financial Management and Control Law).
queries.note: Budget law reference.

queries.text: Which law do paragraphs 2 to 5 of Article 30 of the KVKK relate to?
evidence: (2) – (5) - (It is related to the Law No. 5237 and dated 26/9/2004 and inserted therein)
queries.answer: Law No. 5237 dated 26/9/2004 (the Turkish Penal Code).
queries.note: Thin article (amending provisions only); asks which law paras 2-5 relate to.

queries.text: Who brings into force the by-laws implementing the KVKK?
evidence: By-laws related to the implementation of this Law shall be brought into force by the Authority.
queries.answer: The Personal Data Protection Authority.
queries.note: Who issues implementing by-laws; contrast art. 25(5).

queries.text: How long after the Law's publication did the KVKK's request and complaint provisions enter into force?
evidence: Articles 8, 9, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 18 shall enter into force after six months as of the date of its publication.
queries.answer: Six months after publication.
queries.note: Deferred entry into force (6 months).

queries.text: Which articles of the KVKK entered into force later rather than on the publication date?
evidence: Articles 8, 9, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 18 shall enter into force after six months as of the date of its publication.
queries.answer: Articles 8, 9, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 18 (six months after publication).
queries.note: List question: which articles were deferred.

queries.text: Which body executes the provisions of the KVKK?
evidence: The provisions of this law shall be enforced by the Council of Ministers.
queries.answer: The Council of Ministers.
queries.note: Thin article; executing body.

queries.text: Must a customer apply to us before going to the Board, and within how many days at the latest must we conclude that request?
evidence: A complaint shall not be lodged before exhausting the remedy of the request to the data controller pursuant to Article 13.
at the latest within thirty days and free of charge
queries.answer: Yes, the request to the data controller must be exhausted first; the controller must conclude it within thirty days at the latest.
queries.note: Needs exhaustion rule (14) plus the controller's 30-day deadline (13).

queries.text: If our systems are breached and customer data are obtained by others, whom must we inform, and what is the fine range for failing data security obligations?
evidence: the data controller shall communicate the breach to the data subject and notify it to the Board within the shortest time
An administrative fine of 15.000 to 1.000.000 TL shall be imposed on those who fail to fulfil the obligations related to data security as stipulated in Article 12
queries.answer: The data subject and the Board, within the shortest time; the fine for breaching data security obligations is 15,000 to 1,000,000 TL.
queries.note: Breach notification duty (12(5)) + fine range for art. 12 obligations (18(1)(b)).

queries.text: We signed a standard contract for a transfer abroad. Within how many business days must we notify the Authority, and what is the fine if we don't?
evidence: The standard contract shall be notified to the Authority by the data controller or data processor within five business days following its signature.
An administrative fine of 50.000 to 1.000.000 TL shall be imposed on those who fail to fulfil the obligation to notify as stipulated in Article 9(5).
queries.answer: Within five business days of signature; failing the notification duty carries a fine of 50,000 to 1,000,000 TL.
queries.note: Deadline in 9(5) (also aktarim-md-14(5)) + fine in 18(1)(d).

queries.text: At what stage must we inform customers about the processing of their personal data, and what fine applies if we fail to do so?
evidence: At the time when personal data are obtained, the data controller or the person authorised by it is obliged to inform the data subjects
An administrative fine of 5.000 to 100.000 TL shall be imposed on those who fail to fulfil the obligation to inform as stipulated in Article 10
queries.answer: At the time the personal data are obtained; failure carries an administrative fine of 5,000 to 100,000 TL.
queries.note: Timing of the information obligation (10) + fine range (18(1)(a)).

queries.text: If the information we submitted to the Registry changes, when and how must we report it?
evidence: Any changes in the information given pursuant to the third paragraph shall be immediately notified to the Presidency
data controllers shall notify the Authority through VERBIS within seven days of the date of change
queries.answer: The Law says the changes must be notified to the Presidency immediately; the By-law specifies within seven days of the change, through VERBIS.
queries.note: Law says 'immediately', regulation specifies 7 days via VERBIS; answer needs both.

queries.text: In what situation must we erase or anonymise personal data, and is there a criminal consequence for not doing so?
evidence: personal data shall be erased, destructed or anonymized by the data controller, ex officio or on the request of the data subject, in the event that the reasons for the processing no longer exist
Those who do not erase or anonymize personal data as contrary to the provision of Article 7 of this Law shall be punished in accordance with Article 138 of the Law No. 5237.
queries.answer: When the reasons for processing no longer exist, ex officio or on request; failure is punished under Article 138 of the Penal Code (Law No. 5237).
queries.note: Trigger for erasure (7) + criminal consequence (17(2)).

queries.text: What is the term of office of Board members, and was it the same for everyone on the first Board?
evidence: Term of office of the Board members is four years.

The term of office for the first elected President, the Second President, and two members who are determined by ballot, shall be six years; this period shall be four years for the remaining five members.
queries.answer: The general term is four years; but the first President, Second President and two members chosen by ballot served six years, the other five four years.
queries.note: General 4-year term (21(8)) vs 6-year term for first President etc. (transitional art. 1(6)).

queries.text: When data are processed for a crime investigation, which data subject right still remains available, and what does it cover?
evidence: Article 11 regarding the rights of the data subject, excluding the right to claim compensation
to claim compensation for the damage arising from the unlawful processing of his/her personal data.
queries.answer: The right to claim compensation, i.e. to claim compensation for damage arising from unlawful processing of personal data.
queries.note: 28(2) disapplies art. 11 except compensation; 11(ğ) defines that right.

queries.text: If we do not implement the Board's remedy decision within how many days of notification, what fine range do we face?
evidence: This decision shall be implemented without delay and within thirty days at the latest after the notification
An administrative fine of 25.000 to 1.000.000 TL shall be imposed on those who fail to comply with the decisions issued by the Board as stipulated in Article 15
queries.answer: The decision must be implemented within thirty days at the latest; non-compliance with Board decisions carries a fine of 25,000 to 1,000,000 TL.
queries.note: Implementation deadline (15(5)) + fine for non-compliance (18(1)(c)).

queries.text: Who keeps the Data Controllers' Registry, and which unit within the Authority is responsible for managing it?
evidence: Under the supervision of the Board, the Data Controllers’ Registry shall be kept by the Presidency and be made publicly available.
Responsible department for establishment and management of the Registry is Department of Data Management.
queries.answer: The Presidency keeps it, publicly available, under the Board's supervision; the responsible unit is the Department of Data Management.
queries.note: Law names the Presidency; by-law names the specific department.

queries.text: What is the longest periodic disposal interval we can set in our storage and disposal policy?
evidence: This time interval cannot exceed six months in any case.
queries.answer: The periodic disposal interval cannot exceed six months in any case.
queries.note: Crisp numeric cap; 'altı ay' also appears nowhere else in the corpus for this concept.

queries.text: A data controller that is not obliged to prepare a disposal policy: within what period must it dispose of personal data once the erasure obligation arises?
evidence: within three months following the date for obligation of erasure, destruction or anonymization of personal data arises
queries.answer: Within three months following the date the obligation arises.
queries.note: Three-month deadline for controllers without a policy; must not be confused with the six-month cap or 30-day request deadline.

queries.text: A bank that has a disposal policy: at what point must it dispose of data that have become subject to erasure?
evidence: in the first periodic disposal process following the date when obligation of erasure, destruction or anonymization of personal data arises
queries.answer: In the first periodic disposal process following the date the erasure obligation arises.
queries.note: Timing for controllers with a policy is tied to 'first periodic disposal', not a fixed number of days.

queries.text: In what circumstances can the Board shorten the time limits for ex officio disposal?
evidence: Board may shorten the durations specified in this Article in the case of irreparable or impossible damages, and in the event of explicit infringement of the law.
queries.answer: In the case of irreparable or impossible damages and explicit infringement of the law.
queries.note: Conditions for the Board shortening deadlines; two cumulative-sounding conditions.

queries.text: Who decides the periodic disposal interval, and where must it be set out?
evidence: Time interval for periodic disposal shall be defined in personal data storage and disposal policy by the data controller.
queries.answer: The data controller, in its personal data storage and disposal policy.
queries.note: Casual TR without diacritics. Asks who sets the interval and where.

queries.text: For at least how many years must we keep the records of our disposal operations?
evidence: those records shall be stored for minimum three years excluding other legal obligations
queries.answer: At least three years, excluding other legal obligations.
queries.note: Casual TR without diacritics; three-year minimum retention of disposal logs.

queries.text: Do we only need to log erasures done at a customer's request, or all disposal operations?
evidence: All operations relating to erasure, destruction and anonymization of personal data shall be recorded
queries.answer: All operations relating to erasure, destruction and anonymization must be recorded.
queries.note: Scope of logging duty: all operations, not only request-based ones.

queries.text: Under the erasure by-law, erasure becomes necessary when the processing conditions in which articles of the Law have ceased to exist?
evidence: in the event that all of the conditions for processing laid down in Article 5 and Article 6 of the Law no longer exist
queries.answer: When all of the processing conditions in Articles 5 and 6 of the Law no longer exist.
queries.note: Needs the specific Law articles (5 and 6) cited only in the by-law, not in Law art. 7.

queries.text: Who decides which of erasure, destruction or anonymization is applied?
evidence: Unless otherwise decided by the Board, the data controller may choose one of the appropriate methods
queries.answer: The data controller chooses the appropriate method, unless the Board decides otherwise.
queries.note: Who picks the disposal method; Board override.

queries.text: When disposing of data at a data subject's request, do we have to explain why we chose the method?
evidence: Upon request of data subject, the data controller may choose appropriate method with justified grounds.
queries.answer: Yes, upon request the controller chooses the appropriate method with justified grounds.
queries.note: Request-based disposal requires justification of the chosen method.

queries.text: Where are we required to describe the erasure and anonymization methods we use?
evidence: is obliged to describe the methods used for the erasure, destruction and anonymization operations of personal data in the relevant policies and procedures
queries.answer: In the relevant policies and procedures.
queries.note: Where disposal methods must be documented.

queries.text: What must disposal operations comply with?
evidence: general principles of Article 4 of the Law, technical and organizational measures to be taken within the scope of Article 12, provisions of the relevant legislation, Board decisions and personal data storage and disposal policy
queries.answer: The general principles of Art. 4 of the Law, the technical and organizational measures under Art. 12, relevant legislation, Board decisions and the storage and disposal policy.
queries.note: List question: the rule set disposal must comply with.

queries.text: For data to count as erased, for whom must it become inaccessible?
evidence: the process of rendering personal data inaccessible and non-reusable for the users concerned, by no means
queries.answer: It must be rendered inaccessible and non-reusable for the users concerned, by no means.
queries.note: Erasure standard is relative to 'users concerned', unlike destruction.

queries.text: Does it breach the by-law's definition of erasure if the IT unit responsible for storage and backups can still technically access erased data?
evidence: other than the person or department which is responsible for the technical storage, protection and back up of personal data
the process of rendering personal data inaccessible and non-reusable for the users concerned, by no means
queries.answer: No; erasure means making data inaccessible to the users concerned, and the person or department responsible for technical storage, protection and backup is excluded from 'users concerned'.
queries.note: Needs erasure definition (art. 8, 'users concerned') plus the exclusion of backup/storage units from 'users concerned' (art. 4(b)).

queries.text: What is the key difference between erasure and destruction?
evidence: rendering personal data inaccessible and non-reusable for the users concerned, by no means
Destruction is the process of rendering personal data inaccessible, irretrievable or non-reusable by anyone, by no means.
queries.answer: Erasure makes data inaccessible and non-reusable for the users concerned; destruction makes it inaccessible, irretrievable or non-reusable by anyone.
queries.note: Contrast of two definitions (erasure vs destruction) across two articles.

queries.text: If customers can be re-identified when a dataset is combined with other data, does the dataset count as anonymized?
evidence: rendering personal data impossible to link with an identified or identifiable natural person, even through matching them with other data
queries.answer: No; anonymization means the data cannot be linked to an identified or identifiable person even when matched with other data.
queries.note: Re-identification via linkage defeats anonymization.

queries.text: By which parties must it be impossible to reverse anonymized data?
evidence: such as recovery of data by the data controller, recipient or recipient groups and matching data with other data
queries.answer: By the data controller, the recipient or recipient groups.
queries.note: Names the parties whose reversal attempts must fail.

queries.text: Against what is the appropriateness of anonymization techniques assessed?
evidence: even through using appropriate techniques in respect of the recording medium and relevant field of activity
queries.answer: Their appropriateness for the recording medium and the relevant field of activity.
queries.note: Benchmark for appropriate anonymization techniques.

queries.text: A customer asked for erasure and all processing conditions have ceased; within how many days at most must we conclude the request?
evidence: The data controller shall act on the request of the data subject at the latest within thirty days and inform the data subject.
queries.answer: Within thirty days at the latest, informing the data subject.
queries.note: 30-day deadline for erasure requests; Law art. 13 also has a general 30-day deadline (same answer).

queries.text: In response to a data subject's erasure request, may we anonymize the data instead of erasing it?
evidence: the data controller shall erase, destruct or anonymize the mentioned personal data which are subject to the request
queries.answer: Yes; where all processing conditions have ceased, the controller erases, destroys or anonymizes the data subject to the request.
queries.note: Request-based disposal may be by anonymization too, not just erasure.

queries.text: We had previously transferred the data whose erasure is requested to a business partner; what must we do?
evidence: the data controller shall notify the third party of such request and ensure the performance of necessary operations by the third party within the scope of this By-Law
queries.answer: Notify the third party and ensure the necessary operations are performed by the third party.
queries.note: Third-party transfer scenario.

queries.text: If the processing conditions still exist, can we refuse an erasure request, and how and when must the refusal be communicated?
evidence: such rejection shall be communicated to the data subject in writing or by electronic means at the latest within thirty days
queries.answer: Yes, with justified grounds; the refusal must be communicated in writing or electronically within thirty days at the latest.
queries.note: Refusal path: form and deadline of the rejection.

queries.text: On which articles of the Law does a data subject base a request for erasure of their data?
evidence: When the data subject requests erasure or destruction of his/her personal data from the data controller, pursuant to Article 11 and 13 of the Law
queries.answer: Articles 11 and 13 of the Law.
queries.note: Articles of the Law on which a data subject's erasure request is based.

queries.text: Which data controllers must prepare a personal data storage and disposal policy?
evidence: data controllers who are obliged to register with Data Controllers’ Registry system shall issue personal data storage and disposal policy in accordance with personal data processing inventory
queries.answer: Data controllers obliged to register with the Data Controllers' Registry, in line with their processing inventory.
queries.note: Who must prepare a storage & disposal policy: linked to registry obligation.

queries.text: Does having a storage and disposal policy mean we dispose of data in compliance with the rules?
evidence: To issue personal data storage and disposal policy shall not mean that personal data are stored, erased, destructed or anonymized in accordance with the Law and the By-Law.
queries.answer: No, issuing a policy does not mean data are stored or disposed of in accordance with the Law and the By-Law.
queries.note: Having a policy is not proof of compliance.

queries.text: If we are not required to prepare a policy, does our obligation to erase data also fall away?
evidence: the obligation of storage, erasure, destruction or anonymization of personal data shall continue pursuant to the Law and By-Law
queries.answer: No; the storage, erasure, destruction or anonymization obligations under the Law and the By-Law continue.
queries.note: Casual TR without diacritics; obligations continue without policy duty.

queries.text: Is it mandatory to include periodic disposal periods in the storage and disposal policy?
evidence: Personal data storage and disposal policy shall at least include the following:
Time period for periodic disposal
queries.answer: Yes, the policy must at least include the time period for periodic disposal.
queries.note: Minimum content item (ğ); needs the 'asgari' framing plus the item.

queries.text: What information about staff involved in disposal processes must the policy contain?
evidence: Definitions of titles, units and tasks of those who are involved in personal data storage and disposal processes
queries.answer: The titles, units and task definitions of those involved in storage and disposal processes.
queries.note: Staff-related minimum content item (f).

queries.text: Must the policy present retention and disposal periods in a table?
evidence: Table that shows storage and disposal periods
queries.answer: Yes, a table showing storage and disposal periods is part of the minimum content.
queries.note: Table of retention/disposal periods (g).

queries.text: If we update our existing policy, must the change be shown in the policy?
evidence: Any alterations being made in the current personal data storage and disposal policy, if any.
queries.answer: Yes, any alterations made to the current policy must be included.
queries.note: Change log item (h).

queries.text: What kinds of technical and organizational measures must the storage and disposal policy describe?
evidence: Technical and organizational measures taken against unlawful processing of and access to personal data and for storing personal data securely
Technical and organizational measures taken for lawful disposal of personal data
queries.answer: Measures for secure storage and preventing unlawful processing of and access to data, and measures for lawful disposal of data.
queries.note: Two kinds of measures (d) and (e) must be described.

queries.text: Does the policy need to explain why we store data and why we dispose of it?
evidence: Explanations relating to legal, technical or other reasons requiring storage and disposal of personal data
queries.answer: Yes; it must explain the legal, technical or other reasons requiring storage and disposal.
queries.note: Reasons for storage and disposal (ç).

queries.text: What exactly does the by-law mean by 'disposal'?
evidence: means erasure, destruction or anonymization of personal data
queries.answer: Erasure, destruction or anonymization of personal data.
queries.note: Casual TR without diacritics; definition of 'imha' umbrella term.

queries.text: Does periodic disposal require waiting for a data subject's request?
evidence: to be carried out periodically ex officio
queries.answer: No; periodic disposal is carried out ex officio at recurring intervals set in the policy.
queries.note: Periodic disposal is ex officio and recurring.

queries.text: Should the personal data processing inventory also cover data intended to be transferred abroad and security measures?
evidence: personal data envisaged to be transferred to foreign countries
queries.answer: Yes; the inventory details personal data envisaged to be transferred to foreign countries and data security measures.
queries.note: Inventory definition is identical in both by-laws; both listed.

queries.text: Does the erasure by-law apply only to data processed automatically in digital systems?
evidence: processed wholly or partially by automated means or by non-automated means which provided that form part of a data filing system
queries.answer: No; it also covers data processed by non-automated means that form part of a data filing system.
queries.note: Scope includes non-automated processing within a filing system.

queries.text: To whom do the provisions of the erasure by-law apply?
evidence: shall apply to data controllers in accordance with Article 7 of the Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698
queries.answer: To data controllers, in accordance with Article 7 of the Law.
queries.note: Addressees of the by-law.

queries.text: Which provisions of the Law form the legal basis of the erasure, destruction and anonymization by-law?
evidence: on the basis of Article 7(3) and sub-paragraph (e) of Article 22(1)
queries.answer: Article 7(3) and sub-paragraph (e) of Article 22(1) of the Law.
queries.note: Legal basis; differs from the registry by-law's basis (16(5), 22(1)(d)-(e)).

queries.text: Who is authorised to clarify doubts arising in applying the erasure by-law and to decide on matters it does not cover?
evidence: The Board is authorised to clarify the doubts and recover disruptions to occur during the implementation of this By-Law
queries.answer: The Personal Data Protection Board.
queries.note: Wording identical to registry by-law art. 18 and similar to transfer by-law; question names the erasure by-law.

queries.text: On what date did the by-law on erasure, destruction or anonymization of personal data enter into force?
evidence: This By-Law shall enter into force on 1/1/2018.
queries.note: Same date as the registry by-law (sicil-19); question names this by-law.

queries.text: Who enforces the provisions of the erasure by-law?
evidence: The President of Personal Data Protection Authority shall enforce the provision of this By-Law.
queries.answer: The President of the Personal Data Protection Authority.
queries.note: Enforcement clause; EN names the President of the Authority explicitly.

queries.text: A small brokerage firm that is not obliged to register with the Registry: by when must it dispose of data once the disposal obligation arises?
evidence: data controllers who are obliged to register with Data Controllers’ Registry system shall issue personal data storage and disposal policy
Data controllers who are not obliged to issue personal data storage and disposal policy, shall erase, destruct or anonymize personal data within three months
queries.answer: Since only registry-obliged controllers must prepare a policy, it has no policy obligation and must dispose of the data within three months after the obligation arises.
queries.note: Chain: registry-exempt -> no policy duty (art. 5(1)) -> three-month deadline (art. 11(3)).

queries.text: If banking legislation sets its own rule on erasing or retaining certain records, is that rule taken into account in disposal under the data protection rules?
evidence: The Provisions of other laws relating to the erasure, destruction or anonymization of personal data are reserved.
provisions of the relevant legislation, Board decisions and personal data storage and disposal policy
queries.answer: Yes; the Law reserves provisions of other laws on erasure/destruction/anonymization, and the by-law requires disposal to comply with relevant legislation.
queries.note: Other laws reserved (Law 7(2)) + disposal must follow relevant legislation (by-law 7(2)).

queries.text: When the maximum storage period we declared in VERBIS expires, by when at the latest must we, as a company with a disposal policy, dispose of the data?
evidence: shall be basis for erasure, destruction and anonymization obligations of data controllers specified in Article 7 of the Law
in the first periodic disposal process following the date when obligation of erasure, destruction or anonymization of personal data arises
This time interval cannot exceed six months in any case.
queries.answer: The registered maximum period is the basis for the erasure obligation; once it arises the data must be disposed of at the first following periodic disposal, whose interval cannot exceed six months.
queries.note: Registered maximum period is the erasure trigger (registry by-law 5(ğ)); timing from erasure by-law art. 11.

queries.text: Which two core data protection documents must an insurer that is obliged to register in VERBIS prepare?
evidence: Data controllers under registration obligation are obliged to prepare Personal Data Processing Inventory.
shall issue personal data storage and disposal policy in accordance with personal data processing inventory
queries.answer: A personal data processing inventory and a personal data storage and disposal policy.
queries.note: Two documents from two by-laws: inventory (registry 5(ç)) and disposal policy (erasure 5(1), also registry 9(5)).

queries.text: If the Board exempts us from registration based on annual employee count or balance-sheet size, do we still need a storage and disposal policy and to dispose of data?
evidence: The information of annual number of employees or annual financial balance sheet of the data controller.
data controllers who are obliged to register with Data Controllers’ Registry system shall issue personal data storage and disposal policy
the obligation of storage, erasure, destruction or anonymization of personal data shall continue pursuant to the Law and By-Law
queries.answer: A policy is not required, since that duty applies to registry-obliged controllers; but storage, erasure, destruction or anonymization obligations under the Law and By-Law continue.
queries.note: Exemption by employee/balance-sheet criterion (registry 16(ğ)) -> no policy duty but disposal obligations continue (erasure 5(1),(3)).

queries.text: Is it a problem if we register in VERBIS after we have started processing data?
evidence: Data controllers shall fulfil the obligation to register with the Registry prior to the start of data processing.
queries.answer: Yes; data controllers must register before they start processing personal data.
queries.note: Timing of registration; stated in by-law arts. 5 and 8 and Law art. 16(2).

queries.text: A company not originally obliged to register later becomes obliged; within how many days must it register?
evidence: they shall register with the Registry within thirty days following their entry into the obligation
queries.answer: Within thirty days following its entry into the obligation.
queries.note: 30 days for controllers that become obliged later; distinct from the 30-day extension cap.

queries.text: If a technical impossibility prevents us from registering, by when must we apply to the Authority for extra time?
evidence: apply to the Authority in writing with justifiable grounds in not later than 7 work days
queries.answer: Within 7 work days at the latest, in writing with justified grounds.
queries.note: 7 business days to request extension; easy to confuse with 7-day change notification.

queries.text: What is the maximum extra time the Authority can grant for registration, and how many times?
evidence: Authority may give additional time only once, not exceeding thirty days in any case.
queries.answer: Only once, not exceeding thirty days.
queries.note: Extension: once only, max 30 days.

queries.text: In what situations can extra time be requested for VERBIS registration?
evidence: in cases where they cannot fulfil their obligation to register due to any technical, legal or actual impossibility
queries.answer: Where the registration obligation cannot be fulfilled due to a technical, legal or actual impossibility.
queries.note: Casual TR without diacritics; grounds for extension.

queries.text: Under the registry by-law, if our registered address changes, within how many days and through which channel must we notify it?
evidence: data controllers shall notify the Authority through VERBIS within seven days of the date of change
queries.answer: Within seven days of the change, to the Authority through VERBIS.
queries.note: By-law sets 7 days via VERBIS; the Law (16(4)) says 'immediately' — question anchors on the by-law.

queries.text: We have ended our activity; where do we apply to have our registry record erased?
evidence: The data controller shall apply to the Authority relating to the erasure of their Registry records through VERBIS.
queries.answer: To the Authority, through VERBIS.
queries.note: Deregistration channel.

queries.text: Do erased registry records disappear completely?
evidence: These records shall be accessible in case of any request however they are kept in a manner that no changes can be made.
queries.answer: No; they remain accessible on request but are kept so that no changes can be made.
queries.note: Erased registry records are retained read-only.

queries.text: If our registry record is erased, do our obligations for the period we were registered also end?
evidence: Erasure of registry records does not relieve the data controller of the obligations during the period in which it is registered.
queries.answer: No; erasure of the record does not relieve the controller of obligations for the registered period.
queries.note: Casual TR without diacritics; past obligations survive deregistration.

queries.text: In what case is a registry record erased?
evidence: If the obligation to register is relieved or terminated, Registry records shall be erased.
queries.answer: When the obligation to register is relieved or terminated (the activity requiring registration ends).
queries.note: Trigger for erasure of the record; TR says activity ends, EN says obligation relieved/terminated.

queries.text: Do we have to notify the Registry of processing activities that are necessary to prevent crime or for a criminal investigation?
evidence: Data processing is necessary for the prevention of committing a crime or for crime investigation.
queries.answer: No; there is no obligation to register and notify these activities.
queries.note: Exemption (a); identical case list in Law art. 28(2).

queries.text: Does processing data that the person has made public themselves require notification to VERBIS?
evidence: Processing the data which are made public by the data subject himself/herself.
queries.answer: No; processing data made public by the data subject is exempt from registration and notification.
queries.note: Exemption (b): data made public by the data subject.

queries.text: Is processing necessary to protect the State's financial interests, such as tax and budget matters, exempt from registration?
evidence: Data processing is necessary for protection economic and financial interests of State related to budgetary, tax and financial matters.
queries.answer: Yes; processing necessary to protect the State's economic and financial interests on budget, tax and financial matters is exempt.
queries.note: Exemption (ç): state's budget/tax/financial interests.

queries.text: Can the Board take a company's headcount or balance-sheet size into account when setting registration exemptions?
evidence: The information of annual number of employees or annual financial balance sheet of the data controller.
queries.answer: Yes; the controller's annual number of employees or annual financial balance sheet total is one of the criteria.
queries.note: Criterion added by 2019 amendment; not in Law art. 16(2).

queries.text: Is how long data are kept a criterion in the Board's assessment of registration exemptions?
evidence: Storage period of personal data.
queries.answer: Yes, the storage period of personal data is one of the criteria.
queries.note: Retention period as an exemption criterion (not listed in Law art. 16(2)).

queries.text: How are the Board's decisions on registration exemptions announced?
evidence: Board shall announce such decisions to public via appropriate means of communication.
queries.answer: The Board publishes them and announces them to the public via appropriate means.
queries.note: How exemption decisions are published.

queries.text: Does being exempted from registration by Board decision also lift our other obligations under the Law?
evidence: This derogation shall not remove the obligations of those data controllers under the Law.
queries.answer: No; the derogation does not remove the controller's obligations under the Law.
queries.note: Exemption from registration doesn't lift other Law obligations.

queries.text: Who is responsible for the information published in VERBIS being complete and up to date?
evidence: Data controllers shall be responsible for the information entered into the Registry and published in the Registry to be complete, accurate, up-to-date and lawful.
queries.answer: The data controllers, who are responsible for it being complete, accurate, up-to-date and lawful.
queries.note: Accuracy responsibility for registry data.

queries.text: What role does the information published in the Registry play when preparing privacy notices, responses to requests and explicit consent texts?
evidence: shall be the basis for the obligation to inform for data controllers referred to in Article 10 of the Law, responses to the request of concerned data subjects referred to in Article 13 of the Law and the determination of the scope of explicit consent to be given by data subjects
queries.answer: Information entered based on the inventory and published in the Registry is the basis for the obligation to inform, responses to data subject requests and determining the scope of explicit consent.
queries.note: Registry info as basis for privacy notices, request responses and consent scope.

queries.text: Who determines the scope of and exceptions to the principle that the Registry is public?
evidence: Board is authorized to determine the scope of this principle and derogations provided that the principle of making publicly available is ensured.
queries.answer: The Board, provided that the principle of public availability is ensured.
queries.note: Who defines the scope/exceptions of registry publicity.

queries.text: On which document is the information entered in a VERBIS application based?
evidence: The information to be entered in the application for the Registry is prepared based on Personal Data Processing Inventory.
queries.answer: The Personal Data Processing Inventory.
queries.note: Source document for registry application info.

queries.text: What is the significance of the maximum storage period published in the Registry for erasure and disposal obligations?
evidence: shall be basis for erasure, destruction and anonymization obligations of data controllers specified in Article 7 of the Law
queries.answer: It is the basis for fulfilling the erasure, destruction and anonymization obligations under Article 7 of the Law.
queries.note: Link between registered max storage period and erasure obligations.

queries.text: Which unit of the Authority is responsible for establishing and managing the Registry?
evidence: Responsible department for establishment and management of the Registry is Department of Data Management.
queries.answer: The Department of Data Management.
queries.note: Named department.

queries.text: How often is the Registry activity report submitted to the Board?
evidence: Activity report which has been prepared by Department of Data Management once a three month
queries.answer: Every three months (quarterly).
queries.note: Quarterly activity report; not to be confused with the Authority's annual report (Law art. 20).

queries.text: Who establishes and keeps the Data Controllers' Registry, and who supervises it?
evidence: Registry is established by Presidency.
Supervision of the Registry is carried out by the Board.
queries.answer: The Presidency establishes it; the Board supervises it.
queries.note: Keeper vs supervisor of the Registry; stated in several places.

queries.text: Is information on how long we keep data publicly visible in the Registry?
evidence: Among the information given in the Registry, the following shall be disclosed to the public:
Maximum storage period necessary for the purposes for which personal data are processed.
queries.answer: Yes; the maximum period necessary for the processing purposes is among the publicly disclosed information.
queries.note: Publicity of retention periods.

queries.text: Are the data security measures we have taken published publicly in the Registry?
evidence: Among the information given in the Registry, the following shall be disclosed to the public:
Measures taken for the security of personal data
queries.answer: Yes; measures taken for the security of personal data are among the publicly disclosed information.
queries.note: Casual TR without diacritics; security measures are public.

queries.text: Is our KEP (registered e-mail) address published publicly in the Registry?
evidence: The data controller, representative of the data controller, if any, address and KEP (Registered E-Mail) address, if taken
queries.answer: Yes, if one has been obtained; it is disclosed along with the controller, any representative and address.
queries.note: KEP address published only if obtained.

queries.text: Are the data we plan to transfer abroad publicly visible in the Registry?
evidence: Among the information given in the Registry, the following shall be disclosed to the public:
Personal data which are envisaged to be transferred to foreign countries
queries.answer: Yes; personal data envisaged to be transferred to foreign countries are disclosed to the public.
queries.note: Foreign transfers disclosed publicly (application-content lists in art. 9 and Law 16 are about submission, not publication).

queries.text: Does the registration application include the contact person's identity and address details?
evidence: relating to the identity and address of the data controller, representative of the data controller, if any and contact person
queries.answer: Yes; it includes identity and address information of the controller, any representative and the contact person.
queries.note: Contact person details are part of the application (not in Law art. 16(3)(a)).

queries.text: If the legal retention period for a data category differs from the period we set for business needs, which one do we declare in VERBIS?
evidence: if maximum storage period is envisaged in the legislation, this period shall be entered into the Registry, if not envisaged, the longest storage period of this category shall be entered into the Registry
queries.answer: If the legislation sets a maximum period, that period; otherwise the longest period.
queries.note: Hard: rule for choosing which retention period to declare.

queries.text: Maximum storage periods are reported to the Registry matched with what?
evidence: shall be entered into the Registry by matching them with data categories
queries.answer: With data categories.
queries.note: Retention periods mapped to data categories.

queries.text: When setting the maximum storage period, can we take limitation periods for asserting rights into account?
evidence: Period of limitation determined by the data controller for assertion of a right relating to personal data in the relevant data category.
queries.answer: Yes; the limitation period for asserting a right related to the data is one of the factors considered.
queries.note: Limitation period as a factor.

queries.text: Are retention periods generally accepted in the sector a criterion when setting the maximum period?
evidence: The period generally accepted in the sector in which the data controller operates
queries.answer: Yes; the period generally accepted in the controller's sector is taken into account.
queries.note: Sector practice as a factor.

queries.text: When setting the storage period, are the risks and costs of storage also taken into account?
evidence: The period in which the risks, costs and responsibilities arising from the storage of the relevant data category depending on the purpose of processing shall continue legally
queries.answer: Yes; the period during which the risks, costs and responsibilities of storage legally continue is considered.
queries.note: Casual TR without diacritics; risk/cost factor.

queries.text: What should we do if the predefined headings in VERBIS do not fully cover our activities?
evidence: the data controller shall complete its registration by entering such information into “Others” section in VERBIS
queries.answer: Enter the information in the 'Others' section provided in VERBIS for that purpose to complete the registration.
queries.note: 'Diğer' fallback section in VERBIS.

queries.text: Under the registry by-law, for what purposes do data controllers prepare a storage and disposal policy?
evidence: for defining maximum storage period of personal data for the purposes of processing, complying with this period indicated in personal data processing inventory and tracking whether these periods are exceeded or not
queries.answer: To define the maximum storage period, ensure consistency with the inventory, and track whether the maximum period is exceeded.
queries.note: Purposes of the policy per the registry by-law.

queries.text: What is enough for us to be deemed to have fulfilled the registration obligation?
evidence: Data controllers shall be deemed to have fulfilled its registration obligation by entering the information specified in Article 9 into VERBIS.
queries.answer: Entering the information specified in Article 9 of the by-law into VERBIS.
queries.note: When registration is deemed complete.

queries.text: In a joint-stock company, is the data controller the company itself or an executive such as the general manager?
evidence: Legal persons are themselves the data controllers for the legal persons.
queries.answer: For legal persons, the legal person itself is the data controller.
queries.note: Legal entity is the controller, not its managers.

queries.text: If the board of directors assigns an employee for data protection compliance, does the company's liability fall away?
evidence: This assignment does not remove the responsibilities of legal person pursuant to the provisions of the Law.
queries.answer: No; the assignment does not remove the legal person's responsibility.
queries.note: Delegation doesn't shift liability.

queries.text: Is the contact person authorised to represent the company under the data protection rules?
evidence: Contact person is not authorized to represent data controllers in accordance with the provisions of the Law and the By-law.
queries.answer: No; the contact person is not authorised to represent the data controller under the Law and the By-law.
queries.note: Casual TR without diacritics; contact person cannot represent.

queries.text: In public institutions, at least what level of executive must the contact person be?
evidence: shall be head of department or higher executive
queries.answer: Head of department or a higher executive.
queries.note: Minimum rank of contact person in public institutions.

queries.text: Must the representative of a controller established abroad be authorised to receive the Authority's notifications on its behalf?
evidence: to receive or accept notifications and correspondence made by the Authority on behalf of the data controller
queries.answer: Yes; the designation must at least cover receiving or accepting the Authority's notifications and correspondence on the controller's behalf.
queries.note: Representative's minimum powers: receiving Authority notifications.

queries.text: Who receives data subject requests addressed to a data controller not established in Türkiye on its behalf?
evidence: to receive and transmit requests to be made by data subjects pursuant to first paragraph of the Article 13 of the Law on behalf of the data controller, in case no other principle has been determined by the Board
queries.answer: Unless the Board determines otherwise, the data controller's representative receives and forwards them.
queries.note: Representative receives data subject requests unless Board decides otherwise.

queries.text: At what stage, by whom and in what form is a foreign controller's decision appointing its representative submitted to the Authority?
evidence: shall submit certified copy of decision for the designation of a representative to be taken its competent or person to the Authority during application
queries.answer: A certified copy is submitted by the representative during the registration application.
queries.note: Form of the appointment document.

queries.text: Can a foreign company appoint a natural person who is not a Turkish citizen as its data controller representative in Türkiye?
evidence: the legal person established in Türkiye or the natural person who is citizen of Republic of Türkiye
queries.answer: No; the representative must be a legal person established in Türkiye or a natural person who is a Turkish citizen.
queries.note: Eligibility of representatives.

queries.text: Can a consultancy firm (a legal person) be designated as the contact person?
evidence: “Contact person” means the natural person notified by the data controller
queries.answer: No; the contact person is a natural person notified during registration.
queries.note: Contact person must be a natural person.

queries.text: Under the registry by-law, what kind of e-mail is a KEP address?
evidence: the qualified form of electronic mail which provides legal evidence for the use of it, including sending and delivering of electronic messages
queries.answer: The qualified form of e-mail that provides legal evidence of its use, including sending and delivery.
queries.note: KEP definition.

queries.text: What kind of system is VERBIS, and who establishes and manages it?
evidence: information system that is accessible through the Internet, established and managed by the Presidency
queries.answer: An information system accessible through the Internet, established and managed by the Presidency, used for registration and other Registry operations.
queries.note: VERBIS definition: internet-accessible, run by the Presidency.

queries.text: Through what channel does the Authority communicate with a data controller not established in Türkiye?
evidence: For data controllers not established in Türkiye; representative of the data controller notified to the Registry.
queries.answer: Through the data controller's representative notified to the Registry.
queries.note: Communication with foreign controllers.

queries.text: Which contact details does the Authority use when corresponding with a company established in Türkiye?
evidence: For legal persons established in Türkiye; identity, address or KEP (registered e-mail address) address notified to the Registry
queries.answer: The identity, address or KEP address notified to the Registry.
queries.note: Communication with domestic legal persons.

queries.text: Which provision of the Law sets the administrative fine applied for breaching the registration and notification obligation?
evidence: Administrative fine referred to in sub-paragraph (ç) of Article 18(1) of the Law
queries.answer: Sub-paragraph (ç) of Article 18(1) of the Law.
queries.note: Refers to Law 18(1)(ç) without the amount.

queries.text: What happens if the registration obligation is breached within a public institution?
evidence: the disciplinary provisions shall be applied to the civil servants and other public officers employed in the relevant public institutions and organisations
queries.answer: Upon the Board's notice, disciplinary provisions are applied to the civil servants and public officers concerned and the result is reported to the Board.
queries.note: Public-sector consequence; Law 18(4) is the general version.

queries.text: Who is authorised to clarify doubts in applying the registry by-law and to request any necessary information and documents?
evidence: The Board is authorised to clarify the doubts and recover disruptions to occur during the implementation of this By-law
queries.answer: The Personal Data Protection Board.
queries.note: Wording identical to erasure by-law art. 13; question names the registry by-law.

queries.text: When did the By-Law on the Data Controllers' Registry enter into force?
evidence: This By-law enters into force on 1/1/2018.
queries.note: Same date as erasure by-law (silme-14); question names this by-law.

queries.text: Who is responsible for enforcing the provisions of the registry by-law?
evidence: The President shall enforce the provisions of this By-law.
means the President of Personal Data Protection Authority
queries.answer: The President of the Personal Data Protection Authority.
queries.note: Enforcement clause; 'Başkan' defined in art. 4(b).

queries.text: Whom does the By-Law on the Data Controllers' Registry cover?
evidence: shall apply to natural and legal persons who determine the purposes and means of personal data processing and are responsible for establishment and management of the data filing system
queries.answer: Natural and legal persons who determine the purposes and means of processing and are responsible for establishing and managing the data filing system.
queries.note: Scope of registry by-law.

queries.text: Under which provisions of the Law was the registry (VERBIS) by-law issued?
evidence: on the basis of Article 16(5) and subparagraphs (d) and (e) of Article 22(1) of Law No. 6698
queries.answer: Article 16(5) and sub-paragraphs (d) and (e) of Article 22(1) of the Law.
queries.note: Casual TR without diacritics; legal basis differs from erasure by-law.

queries.text: What is the purpose of the By-Law on the Data Controllers' Registry?
evidence: to determine and ensure the implementation of procedures and principles related to the establishment and management of Data Controllers’ Registry
queries.answer: To set and implement the procedures and principles for establishing and managing the publicly available Registry kept by the Presidency under Board supervision, and for the records to be entered in it.
queries.note: Purpose clause; thin.

queries.text: How do the Law and the by-law regulate the deadline for notifying changes to registry information?
evidence: Any changes in the information given pursuant to the third paragraph shall be immediately notified to the Presidency
data controllers shall notify the Authority through VERBIS within seven days of the date of change
queries.answer: The Law requires changes to be notified immediately to the Presidency; the by-law requires notification to the Authority through VERBIS within seven days of the change.
queries.note: Law says 'immediately' to the Presidency; by-law says 7 days via VERBIS to the Authority. Needs both.

queries.text: How large an administrative fine can be imposed on a company that fails to comply with the VERBIS registration and notification obligation?
evidence: Administrative fine referred to in sub-paragraph (ç) of Article 18(1) of the Law
An administrative fine of 20.000 to 1.000.000 TL shall be imposed on those who act contrary to the obligations for registry with the Data Controllers’ Registry
queries.answer: The registry by-law refers to Article 18(1)(ç) of the Law, which sets an administrative fine of 20,000 to 1,000,000 TL (per the corpus text).
queries.note: By-law points to Law 18(1)(ç); the amount is only in the Law.

queries.text: We cannot complete VERBIS registration in time due to a technical problem; if we get an extension, how long can it be at most and by when must we complete registration?
evidence: Authority may give additional time only once, not exceeding thirty days in any case.
are obliged to complete registration before this time expires
queries.answer: The Authority may grant extra time only once, up to thirty days; the controller must complete the registration before that period expires.
queries.note: Extension limits (art. 8(3)) + must complete within the extension (art. 10(2)).

queries.text: If a group company established abroad will process data of customers in Türkiye, who registers, when, and what document is submitted with the application?
evidence: Data controllers not established in Türkiye are obliged to register with the Registry by their representatives prior to the start of data processing.
shall submit certified copy of decision for the designation of a representative to be taken its competent or person to the Authority during application
queries.answer: It must register through its representative before starting processing; the representative submits a certified copy of the appointment decision during the application.
queries.note: Foreign controller: registers via representative before processing (5(b)) + certified copy of appointment decision (11(2)).

queries.text: For a data category whose retention period is set by legislation, which period do we declare to the Registry, and what obligation is that declared period later the basis for?
evidence: if maximum storage period is envisaged in the legislation, this period shall be entered into the Registry
shall be basis for erasure, destruction and anonymization obligations of data controllers specified in Article 7 of the Law
queries.answer: The maximum period set by the legislation; the published maximum period is the basis for the erasure, destruction and anonymization obligations under Article 7 of the Law.
queries.note: Which period to declare (9(4)) and what that declared period then governs (5(ğ)).

queries.text: Which article of the KVKK is the by-law on transferring personal data abroad meant to implement?
evidence: establish the procedures and principles regarding the implementation of Article 9 of the Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698
queries.answer: Article 9 of Law No. 6698, which regulates the transfer of personal data abroad.
queries.note: Easy; purpose clause, answer is a single article number.

queries.text: Does the by-law on transfers abroad bind only data controllers, or are data processors covered as well?
evidence: shall apply to data controllers and data processors involved in the transfer of personal data abroad
queries.answer: Both: it applies to data controllers and data processors involved in the transfer abroad under Article 9 of the Law.
queries.note: Scope; checks that processors are covered too, not only controllers.

queries.text: Which provisions of the Law does the by-law on transfers abroad rely on as its legal basis?
evidence: This By-Law is issued pursuant to Article 9(11) and Article 22(1)(e) of the Law No. 6698.
queries.answer: Article 9(11) and Article 22(1)(e) of Law No. 6698.
queries.note: Legal basis; precise paragraph/subparagraph citation.

queries.text: What term does the by-law use for the counterparty that receives the data abroad, and who can it be?
evidence: Data importer: A data controller or data processor in a foreign country receiving personal data from the data exporter
queries.answer: Data importer: a data controller or data processor in a foreign country receiving personal data from the data exporter.
queries.note: Definition of data importer; question avoids the term itself.

queries.text: If we don't send the data to a group company abroad but only give it remote access to our systems, does that still count as a transfer abroad?
evidence: to a data controller or data processor established abroad, or making such data accessible to them by any other means
queries.answer: Yes. Under the definition, making the data accessible to a controller or processor abroad by any other means is also a transfer abroad, not only transmitting it.
queries.note: Hard-ish: remote access (no copying) counts as transfer via 'making accessible by other means'.

queries.text: Under the by-law, can the party exporting data abroad only be a data controller?
evidence: Data exporter: A data controller or data processor transferring personal data abroad
queries.answer: No. The data exporter is the data controller or data processor transferring personal data abroad.
queries.note: Definition of data exporter; yes/no form.

queries.text: For a term that the by-law on transfers abroad does not define, which definition applies?
evidence: For the definitions not covered in this By-Law, the definitions provided in the Law and relevant legislation shall apply.
queries.answer: The definitions in the Law and the relevant legislation apply.
queries.note: Casual TR without diacritics; fallback-definitions rule.

queries.text: As a data processor transferring data abroad, is complying with the Law and the by-law enough, or what else must we follow?
evidence: In cases where personal data is transferred by the processor, the instructions from the controller shall also be complied with.
queries.answer: It is not enough; the processor must also comply with the controller's instructions.
queries.note: Processor must also follow controller's instructions; stated in both art. 5(1) and art. 7(1).

queries.text: If the importer abroad passes the data it received from us on to a third country, do the transfer-abroad rules also apply to that onward transfer?
evidence: The provision of the first paragraph shall also apply to onward transfers of personal data that has been transferred abroad, and transfers to international organisations.
queries.answer: Yes. The same procedures and principles apply to onward transfers of data already transferred abroad and to transfers to international organisations.
queries.note: Onward transfers; same answer in reg. art. 5(2) and Law art. 9(8).

queries.text: If another law, such as banking legislation, has its own provision on transferring data abroad, do the KVKK transfer rules override it?
evidence: The provisions of other laws concerning the transfer of personal data abroad are reserved.
queries.answer: No. Provisions of other laws concerning the transfer of personal data abroad are reserved.
queries.note: Other laws reserved; identical in reg. art. 5(3) and Law art. 9(10).

queries.text: If we transfer data to a country with an adequacy decision, do we also need one of the processing conditions in Article 5 or 6 of the Law?
evidence: Personal data may be transferred abroad by controllers and processors under one of the conditions specified in Article 5 and Article 6 of the Law, and in the event of the following circumstances
queries.answer: Yes. The transfer requires one of the conditions in Article 5 or 6 of the Law in addition to the adequacy decision (or another listed circumstance).
queries.note: Adequacy alone is not enough; an Art. 5/6 processing condition is also required.

queries.text: Without an adequacy decision, if we rely on an appropriate safeguard, what additional condition applies regarding the destination country?
evidence: that data subject rights and effective legal remedies for data subjects are also available in the country receiving the transfer
queries.answer: Data subjects must also be able to exercise their rights and have effective legal remedies in the destination country.
queries.note: Extra destination-country condition for safeguard-based transfers; stated in three provisions.

queries.text: Where the interests of Türkiye or the data subject would be seriously harmed, under what condition may data still be transferred abroad?
evidence: personal data may only be transferred abroad with the permission of the Board by obtaining the opinion of the relevant public institution or organisation
queries.answer: Without prejudice to international conventions, only with the Board's permission after obtaining the opinion of the relevant public institution or organisation.
queries.note: Serious-harm transfers: Board permission after public body opinion.

queries.text: Does a processor transferring data abroad leave security measures to the controller, or must it take them itself?
evidence: The processor shall implement all necessary technical and organisational measures to ensure an appropriate level of security, corresponding to the nature of personal data
queries.answer: The processor itself must take all necessary technical and organisational measures to ensure a security level appropriate to the nature of the data.
queries.note: Processor's own security obligations when transferring abroad.

queries.text: If our processor carries out the transfer abroad, are we as controller relieved of our compliance responsibility?
evidence: The transfer of personal data abroad by the processor shall not relieve the controller of its responsibility to comply with the procedures and principles, and to ensure the necessary safeguards
queries.answer: No. A transfer by the processor does not relieve the controller of its responsibility to follow the procedures and ensure the safeguards.
queries.note: Controller not relieved of responsibility when processor transfers.

queries.text: If the duty to notify the standard contract falls on the processor, should the processor wait for the controller's instruction?
evidence: the processor shall fulfil this notification obligation independently of any instructions from the controller
queries.answer: No. The processor fulfils the notification obligation independently of any instructions from the controller.
queries.note: Processor notifies standard contract without waiting for controller instruction.

queries.text: Is the controller also responsible for whether the processor takes the necessary technical and organisational measures in a transfer abroad?
evidence: The controller shall be obliged to ensure that the technical and organisational measures specified in the first paragraph are implemented by the processor.
queries.answer: Yes. The controller is obliged to ensure that the processor implements those measures.
queries.note: Controller's duty to ensure processor's measures.

queries.text: Is an adequacy decision only issued for a whole country, or can it also cover specific sectors within a country?
evidence: The Board may decide that a country, one and more sectors within that country, or an international organisation offers an adequate level of protection
queries.answer: The Board may decide adequacy for a country, one or more sectors within it, or an international organisation.
queries.note: Adequacy can be sector-specific; Board decides.

queries.text: Is the Board limited to the factors listed in the by-law when assessing adequacy?
evidence: The Board shall be authorised to determine additional factors beyond those specified in the first paragraph.
queries.answer: No. The Board is authorised to determine additional factors beyond those listed.
queries.note: Board may add adequacy criteria beyond the list; only in the regulation.

queries.text: Apart from the Official Gazette, where else are adequacy decisions published?
evidence: Adequacy decisions issued by the Board shall be published in the Official Gazette and on the Authority’s website.
queries.answer: On the Authority's website as well.
queries.note: Publication venue beyond the Official Gazette; Law art. 9 only mentions the Gazette, so question is made specific.

queries.text: In the adequacy assessment, is it considered whether the other country has an independent data protection authority and administrative/judicial redress?
evidence: The existence of an independent and effective data protection authority in the country or to which an international organisation is subject, as well as the availability of administrative and judicial redress
queries.answer: Yes. The existence of an independent and effective data protection authority and of administrative and judicial redress is one of the factors taken into account.
queries.note: Adequacy factor: DPA and redress; identical in reg. and Law.

queries.text: At most how many years can pass before an adequacy decision is re-evaluated?
evidence: The adequacy decision shall be re-evaluated at least every four years.
queries.answer: Four years; it is re-evaluated at least every four years.
queries.note: Casual TR; numeric (4 years); same in reg. and Law.

queries.text: How can one tell when a particular adequacy decision will be re-evaluated?
evidence: The adequacy decision in question shall explicitly specify the re-evaluation periods.
queries.answer: The re-evaluation periods are explicitly specified in the adequacy decision itself.
queries.note: Where re-evaluation periods are set; only in the regulation.

queries.text: If the Board revokes an adequacy decision for a country, does the revocation have retroactive effect?
evidence: may amend, suspend, or revoke the decision with prospective effect
queries.answer: No. The Board may amend, suspend or revoke an adequacy decision only with prospective effect.
queries.note: Prospective effect of revocation; 'what happens if' form.

queries.text: If a country's adequacy decision is suspended, can the Board talk to that country's authorities to fix the problem?
evidence: The Board may consult with the competent authorities of the relevant country or international organisation to remedy the circumstances that led to the amendment, suspension, or revocation of the adequacy decision
queries.answer: Yes. The Board may consult the competent authorities of the country or international organisation to remedy the circumstances that led to the amendment, suspension or revocation.
queries.note: Board consultation with foreign authorities after suspension; only in regulation.

queries.text: Where can we follow whether the adequacy decision for a country we transfer to has been suspended or revoked?
evidence: The decisions concerning the amendment, suspension, or revocation of the adequacy decision shall be published in the Official Gazette and on the Authority’s website.
queries.answer: Such decisions are published in the Official Gazette and on the Authority's website.
queries.note: Publication of suspension/revocation decisions.

queries.text: Between which companies can binding corporate rules be used as an appropriate safeguard?
evidence: Appropriate safeguards may be provided through binding corporate rules for the protection of personal data, which the companies within the group of undertakings engaged in joint economic activity are obliged to comply with.
queries.answer: Among the companies within a group of undertakings engaged in joint economic activity.
queries.note: Who can use BCRs: group of undertakings in joint economic activity.

queries.text: Between which parties can an agreement not classified as an international convention be used as an appropriate safeguard?
evidence: for the transfer of personal data between public institutions and organisations, or professional organisations with public institution status in Türkiye, and public institutions, organisations, or international organisations abroad
queries.answer: Between public institutions and organisations or professional organisations with public institution status in Türkiye and public institutions, organisations or international organisations abroad.
queries.note: Parties eligible for non-international-convention agreements (public bodies only).

queries.text: What element does the Board's standard contract contain with respect to sensitive personal data?
evidence: additional measures for sensitive personal data
queries.answer: Additional measures for sensitive personal data.
queries.note: Content of the Board's standard contract regarding sensitive data.

queries.text: Is signing a written commitment with the importer abroad enough for the transfer, or is the Board's permission also required?
evidence: The existence of a written commitment containing provisions to ensure adequate protections, and approval for the transfer by the Board.
queries.answer: The Board's permission is also required: both the written commitment and the Board's approval of the transfer are needed.
queries.note: Written commitment needs Board permission (unlike standard contract).

queries.text: As a public institution negotiating a data transfer agreement with a foreign public body, do we need to consult the Board at this stage?
evidence: The Board’s opinion shall be sought during the negotiation process of the agreement.
queries.answer: Yes. The Board's opinion is sought during the negotiation of the agreement.
queries.note: Board opinion during negotiation of public-sector agreement.

queries.text: For a transfer based on such an agreement, who applies to the Board for permission?
evidence: To transfer the personal data abroad based on the agreement, the data exporter shall apply to the Board for permission.
queries.answer: The data exporter.
queries.note: Casual TR; who files permission for agreement-based transfers.

queries.text: When applying for permission for an agreement-based transfer, should a draft of the agreement be submitted to the Board, or which version?
evidence: the final version of the agreement text and any other information and documents necessary for the Board’s evaluation shall be submitted to the Board
queries.answer: The final version of the agreement text, with the other information and documents needed for the Board's evaluation.
queries.note: Final text vs draft in the permission application.

queries.text: If the counterparty fails to comply with the agreement's data protection provisions, what right must the agreement give the exporting party?
evidence: A provision granting the data exporter the right to suspend the data transfer and terminate the agreement
queries.answer: The right of the data exporter to suspend the data transfer and terminate the agreement.
queries.note: Casual TR; exporter's suspend/terminate right in agreement.

queries.text: When an agreement not classified as an international convention ends, what must the importer abroad do with the data it holds?
evidence: to either return the personal data transferred, including all backups, to the data exporter or to completely destroy such data, at the choice of the data exporter
queries.answer: At the data exporter's choice, return the data with all backups or completely destroy it.
queries.note: Return-or-destroy on termination, at exporter's choice.

queries.text: Must a data transfer agreement between public bodies include arrangements for auditing compliance with its data protection provisions?
evidence: An auditing mechanism to ensure compliance with the data protection provisions to be included the agreement
queries.answer: Yes. The agreement must include an auditing mechanism for compliance with its data protection provisions.
queries.note: Audit mechanism required in the public-sector agreement.

queries.text: In a BCR approval application, can we submit our group headquarters' English documents without translation?
evidence: If any document submitted for the application is in a foreign language, a notarised translation shall be attached to the application.
queries.answer: No. A notarised translation of each foreign-language document must be attached to the application.
queries.note: BCR application: foreign-language documents need notarised translation.

queries.text: If the BCR text is prepared in both Turkish and English, which version prevails?
evidence: If the binding corporate rules are also prepared in a foreign language, the Turkish text shall prevail.
queries.answer: The Turkish text prevails.
queries.note: Language precedence for BCR text.

queries.text: After filing the BCR application, can we start intra-group transfers without waiting for the Board's approval?
evidence: The transfer of personal data may only commence after the Board has approved the binding corporate rules.
queries.answer: No. Transfers may only begin after the Board has approved the binding corporate rules.
queries.note: Timing: transfers only after BCR approval.

queries.text: When approving BCRs, does the Board require the rules to be binding on the group companies' employees as well?
evidence: legally binding and enforceable for each relevant member within the group of undertakings engaged in joint economic activity, including their employees
queries.answer: Yes. The rules must be legally binding and enforceable for each relevant member of the group, including their employees.
queries.note: Approval criterion: binding on each member including employees.

queries.text: If a group company outside Türkiye breaches the binding corporate rules, who assumes liability under the BCR?
evidence: in the event of a breach of the binding corporate rules by any member not established in Türkiye, a controller and/or processor established in Türkiye will assume liability for the breach
queries.answer: A controller and/or processor established in Türkiye assumes liability for the breach.
queries.note: Liability of a Türkiye-established entity for breaches by foreign group members.

queries.text: Which staff must the data protection training commitment in the BCR specifically cover?
evidence: A commitment to provide appropriate data protection training to personnel having permanent or regular access to personal data
queries.answer: Personnel having permanent or regular access to personal data.
queries.note: Training commitment scope (permanent/regular access staff).

queries.text: To whom must the internal audit and verification results under the BCR be communicated?
evidence: a commitment that such results will be communicated to the person or entity referred to in subparagraph (ğ) and to the board of the controlling company within the relevant group of undertakings, and to the Board upon request
queries.answer: To the person or entity monitoring BCR compliance, to the board of the controlling company of the group, and to the Board upon request.
queries.note: Recipients of BCR audit results (three recipients, one conditional).

queries.text: If a legislative change in the destination country could adversely affect the BCR safeguards, what must the BCR provide for?
evidence: mechanisms to notify the Board in case of a legislative change which likely to have a substantial adverse effect on these guarantees
queries.answer: Mechanisms to notify the Board of the situation.
queries.note: Adverse legislative change in destination country: notify the Board.

queries.text: If we change the approved BCR text, do the changes have to be reported to the Board?
evidence: The mechanisms for reporting and recording changes to the binding corporate rules and reporting those changes to the Board
queries.answer: Yes. The BCR must contain mechanisms for reporting and recording changes and reporting them to the Board.
queries.note: Changes to BCR must be reported/recorded and notified to Board.

queries.text: Must the BCR also guarantee that data subjects whose data is transferred can complain to the Board?
