evidence: their right to lodge a complaint with the Board in accordance with the procedures and principles outlined in Article 14 of the Law
queries.answer: Yes. It must include a commitment to enable the right to lodge a complaint with the Board under Article 14 of the Law.
queries.note: Complaint right to the Board must be guaranteed in BCR.

queries.text: Must the BCR text include the group companies' organisational structure and contact details?
evidence: The organisational structure and contact details for each member of the group of undertakings engaged in a joint economic activity
queries.answer: Yes. The organisational structure and contact details of each group member are part of the minimum content.
queries.note: Casual TR; organisational structure and contact details of each member.

queries.text: Within how many days after signing must we notify the standard contract to the Authority?
evidence: The standard contract, after finalisation of the signatures, shall be notified to the Authority within five business days
queries.answer: Within five business days after the signatures are finalised.
queries.note: Classic deadline: 5 business days; reg. counts from completion of signatures.

queries.text: Through which channels can the standard contract be notified to the Authority?
evidence: either physically, through a registered electronic mail (KEP) address, or via other methods specified by the Board
queries.answer: Physically, via a registered electronic mail (KEP) address, or by other methods specified by the Board.
queries.note: Notification channels (physical, KEP, other Board methods).

queries.text: If the standard contract doesn't say who will notify it, who has to notify the Authority?
evidence: If no such agreement is made, the data exporter shall be responsible for notifying the Board.
queries.answer: The data exporter.
queries.note: Casual TR; default notifier is the data exporter.

queries.text: Can we add clauses to or remove provisions from the standard contract to suit our business needs?
evidence: The standard contract text shall be used without any modifications.
queries.answer: No. The standard contract text must be used without any modifications.
queries.note: No modification of standard contract text.

queries.text: What happens if the standard contract text has been modified or one party's valid signature is missing?
evidence: the Board shall conduct an examination in accordance with Article 15 of the Law
queries.answer: The Board conducts an examination under Article 15 of the Law.
queries.note: Consequence: Board examination under Law art. 15.

queries.text: Which documents must be attached to the standard contract notification?
evidence: The notification shall include documents certifying that the signatories are authorised, along with notarised translations of any foreign language documents.
queries.answer: Documents proving the signatories are authorised, and notarised translations of any foreign-language documents.
queries.note: Attachments to the notification.

queries.text: If the parties to the standard contract change or the contract ends, does the Authority need to be notified again?
evidence: or if the standard contract is expired, the Board shall be notified in accordance with the procedure outlined in paragraph five
queries.answer: Yes. The Board must be notified following the same procedure as in paragraph five.
queries.note: Re-notification on party change or expiry.

queries.text: If we also sign the standard contract in English with the counterparty, which language version prevails?
evidence: In the event the standard contract is also concluded in a foreign language, the Turkish text shall prevail.
queries.answer: The Turkish text prevails.
queries.note: Language precedence for standard contract.

queries.text: Which law must a written commitment with the importer abroad be subject to, and which courts must have jurisdiction in a dispute?
evidence: A commitment confirming that the commitment letter is subject to Turkish law and, in case of a dispute, Turkish courts shall have jurisdiction
queries.answer: Turkish law, with Turkish courts having jurisdiction, and the importer agreeing to recognise that jurisdiction.
queries.note: Governing law and forum in the written commitment.

queries.text: Must the importer abroad commit in the written commitment to comply with the Board's decisions?
evidence: A commitment by the data importer to comply with the Board’s decisions and opinions regarding the processing of personal data subject to the transfer
queries.answer: Yes. The importer must commit to comply with the Board's decisions and opinions on processing the transferred data.
queries.note: Importer's commitment to Board decisions; only in commitment letter list.

queries.text: Under the commitment letter, to whom and when must the importer report a possible legislative change in its country that could prevent compliance?
evidence: a commitment to notify the data exporter as soon as possible of any potential legislative changes that may lead to such a failure
queries.answer: To the data exporter, as soon as possible.
queries.note: Timing and recipient of legislative-change notice under commitment letter.

queries.text: We have signed the commitment letter with the importer abroad; can we start transferring the data right away?
evidence: To transfer personal data abroad based on the commitment letter, data exporter shall apply to the Board for permission.
The transfer of personal data may only commence after the Board has granted permission.
queries.answer: No. The data exporter must apply to the Board for permission, and transfers may start only after the Board grants it.
queries.note: Commitment letter signed != can start; needs exporter's application and Board permission.

queries.text: Must the commitment letter set out the remedies available to data subjects if it is breached?
evidence: A redress mechanism available to data subjects in the event of a breach of the commitment letter
queries.answer: Yes. It must include the redress mechanisms available to data subjects in case of breach.
queries.note: Casual TR; redress methods in commitment letter.

queries.text: What does the 'incidental' requirement for exceptional transfers abroad mean; which transfers count as incidental?
evidence: Transfers that are not regular, occur only once or a few times, do not have a continues nature, and are not part of the ordinary course of business shall be considered incidental.
queries.answer: Transfers that are not regular, happen only once or a few times, are not continuous, and are not part of the ordinary course of business.
queries.note: Definition of 'incidental' exists only in the regulation, not in the Law.

queries.text: If we rely on explicit consent for an exceptional transfer abroad, what must the customer be informed about beforehand?
evidence: The data subject has given explicit consent to the transfer, provided that he/she has been informed of the potential risks involved
queries.answer: The potential risks involved in the transfer.
queries.note: Explicit consent exception requires risk information; same in Law 9(6)(a).

queries.text: When making an exceptional transfer abroad from a public registry, may all the data in the registry be transferred?
evidence: The transfer shall not include all personal data or categories of personal data contained within the registries
queries.answer: No. The transfer may not include all personal data or data categories in the registry.
queries.note: Registry-based exceptional transfers cannot cover the whole registry; only in regulation.

queries.text: From a registry open only to persons with a legitimate interest, to whom can a transfer abroad be made?
evidence: Transfers from registries accessible to persons with legitimate interests shall only be made to those persons or upon their request.
queries.answer: Only to those persons with a legitimate interest, or upon their request.
queries.note: Legitimate-interest registries: only to those persons or at their request.

queries.text: Can a public institution, in its public-law activities, make an exceptional transfer abroad based on the data subject's explicit consent?
evidence: The provisions in subparagraphs (a), (b), and (c) of the second paragraph shall not apply to the activities of public law activities of public institutions and organisations.
queries.answer: No. The consent and contract exceptions (subparagraphs a, b and c) do not apply to public-law activities of public institutions.
queries.note: Public bodies can't use consent/contract exceptions for public-law activities.

queries.text: Without any safeguard, can an incidental transfer abroad that is necessary to perform our contract with the customer fall under an exception?
evidence: The transfer is necessary for the performance of a contract between the data subject and the controller
queries.answer: Yes. Necessity for performing a contract between the data subject and the controller is one of the exceptional cases, provided the transfer is incidental.
queries.note: Contract-performance exception; same wording in Law 9(6)(b).

queries.text: Is transferring an unconscious customer's data to a hospital abroad to save their life covered by an exception?
evidence: Transfer of personal data is necessary for the protection of life or physical integrity of the person himself/herself or of any other person, who is unable to explain his/her consent due to the physical disability
queries.answer: Yes. A transfer necessary to protect the life or physical integrity of a person unable to give consent is an exceptional case, provided it is incidental.
queries.note: Casual TR; vital-interest exception.

queries.text: If a doubt arises in applying the by-law on transfers abroad, or a matter isn't covered by it, who decides?
evidence: The Board shall be authorised to resolve any ambiguities that may arise in the implementation of this By-Law and to make decisions on matters not specifically addressed within herein
queries.answer: The Board (Personal Data Protection Board).
queries.note: Thin provision; sibling regulations have similar clauses, question names the transfer by-law.

queries.text: Did the by-law on transfers abroad have a transition period, or did it enter into force on the day it was published?
evidence: This By-Law shall enter into force on the date of its publication.
queries.answer: It entered into force on the date of its publication.
queries.note: Thin provision; no date in corpus, only 'on publication'. Sibling regulations have near-identical clauses.

queries.text: Who is responsible for executing the provisions of the by-law on transfers abroad?
evidence: The President of the Personal Data Protection Authority shall be responsible for executing the provisions of this By-Law.
queries.answer: The President of the Personal Data Protection Authority.
queries.note: Thin provision; executor is the Authority's President (not the Board).

queries.text: The standard contract designates us, the processor, to make the notification; should we wait for the controller's instruction, and within how many days must we notify?
evidence: the processor shall fulfil this notification obligation independently of any instructions from the controller
The standard contract, after finalisation of the signatures, shall be notified to the Authority within five business days
queries.answer: No instruction is needed; the processor notifies on its own. The deadline is five business days after the signatures are finalised.
queries.note: Needs art. 7(3) (no instruction needed) + art. 14(5) (5 business days).

queries.text: What condition does Article 9 of the Law attach to exceptional transfers when no safeguard exists, and how does the by-law define that condition?
evidence: may transfer personal data abroad only under one of the circumstances specified below, provided that such transfer is incidental
Transfers that are not regular, occur only once or a few times, do not have a continues nature, and are not part of the ordinary course of business shall be considered incidental.
queries.answer: The transfer must be incidental; incidental transfers are those that are not regular, occur once or a few times, are not continuous and are not part of the ordinary course of business.
queries.note: Law 9(6) sets the incidental requirement without defining it; reg. art. 16(1) defines it.

queries.text: What is submitted to the Board in a BCR approval application, and who determines which documents are to be used?
evidence: As part of the application, the text of the binding corporate rules and any other information and documents necessary for the Board’s evaluation shall be submitted to the Board.
The documents required for the application of binding corporate rules shall be determined by the Board.
queries.answer: The BCR text and other information and documents needed for the Board's evaluation (foreign-language documents with notarised translation); the Board determines the required documents.
queries.note: BCR application contents (art. 12(2)) + Board sets required documents (art. 13(2)).

queries.text: The processor performs the transfer and the standard contract doesn't say who will notify; who notifies the Authority in that case?
evidence: If no such agreement is made, the data exporter shall be responsible for notifying the Board.
Data exporter: A data controller or data processor transferring personal data abroad
queries.answer: The processor. Absent a designation the data exporter notifies, and a processor carrying out the transfer is by definition the data exporter.
queries.note: Default notifier is the 'data exporter' (art. 14(5)); art. 4 shows a processor can be the exporter.

queries.text: If our importer abroad is going to pass the data on to another country with no adequacy decision, does that onward transfer also need an appropriate safeguard?
evidence: The provision of the first paragraph shall also apply to onward transfers of personal data that has been transferred abroad, and transfers to international organisations.
but only where one of the following appropriate safeguards is provided by the parties involved in the transfer
queries.answer: Yes. The same rules apply to onward transfers; without adequacy, one of the appropriate safeguards (non-convention agreement, BCR, standard contract, written commitment) must be in place.
queries.note: Onward-transfer rule (art. 5(2) or Law 9(8)) + safeguards when no adequacy (art. 10 or Law 9(4)).

queries.text: In terms of when transfers may begin, how does a commitment letter differ from a standard contract?
evidence: The transfer of personal data may only commence after the Board has granted permission.
The standard contract, after finalisation of the signatures, shall be notified to the Authority within five business days
queries.answer: Under a commitment letter the exporter applies for Board permission and transfers start only after it is granted; for a standard contract no permission is provided for, it is notified to the Authority within five business days after signature.
queries.note: Compare start conditions: commitment letter needs Board permission; standard contract only notification.

queries.text: If the adequacy decision for the country we transfer to is suspended, on what basis can we continue transfers?
evidence: it may amend, suspend, or revoke its decision with prospective effect

In the absence of an adequacy decision, one of the appropriate safeguards specified in Article 10 is provided by the parties, on the condition that data subject rights and effective legal remedies for data subjects are also available in the country receiving the transfer.
only under one of the exceptional circumstances specified in Article 16, provided that such transfer is incidental
queries.answer: Suspension has prospective effect; thereafter one of the Article 10 safeguards is needed (provided data subjects have rights and remedies there), and failing that only the Article 16 exceptions for incidental transfers.
queries.note: Suspension is prospective (art. 9); then fall back to safeguards or incidental exceptions (art. 6).

queries.text: We transfer sensitive data within the group under BCRs and outside the group under the standard contract; must both instruments include additional measures for sensitive data?
evidence: adequate measures for processing sensitive personal data
additional measures, and additional measures for sensitive personal data
queries.answer: Yes. The BCR minimum content includes adequate measures for processing sensitive data, and the standard contract includes additional measures for sensitive personal data.
queries.note: Sensitive-data measures appear in both BCR minimum content and standard contract content.

queries.text: We will give a consultancy abroad one-off access to our database; with no adequacy decision or safeguard, does this access count as a transfer, and under what condition is it possible?
evidence: to a data controller or data processor established abroad, or making such data accessible to them by any other means
Transfers that are not regular, occur only once or a few times, do not have a continues nature, and are not part of the ordinary course of business shall be considered incidental.
queries.answer: Yes, making data accessible is a transfer abroad. Being one-off it can be incidental, but one of the Article 16 exceptional cases must still apply.
queries.note: Remote access = transfer (art. 4) + one-off access can be incidental but still needs an art. 16 exception.

queries.text: Regarding the Board's involvement, how does an agreement not classified as an international convention differ from a commitment letter?
evidence: The Board’s opinion shall be sought during the negotiation process of the agreement.
To transfer personal data abroad based on the commitment letter, data exporter shall apply to the Board for permission.
queries.answer: In both the data exporter applies to the Board for permission and transfers start after it is granted; for the agreement the Board's opinion is additionally sought during negotiation.
queries.note: Compare Board involvement: both need exporter's permission application; agreement also needs Board opinion during negotiation.
